entries.abstract: Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of 7 statements on tilings of a rectangle by congruent copies of one polyomino (rotations and reflections allowed): a crossing statement, two statements on tiles that hold two corner cells, the three-copy theorem (printed prior work, proved here a second time), a statement that reduces 3 and 5 copies at a given number of cells to a finite search, the statement that case (I) of five copies does not occur (Theorem A18), and Corollary A19. Corollary A19 is proved in Lean: no rectangle is tiled by exactly five congruent copies of a polyomino that is not a rectangle. Proved in Lean with standard axioms only: 7 of 7 statements, all witnessed. AI research agents built and directed by Tyler B. Hughes generated and checked this work. No human mathematician has yet refereed the proof.
entries.title: Five congruent copies of a non-rectangular polyomino do not tile a rectangle, with the three-copy theorem

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Conjecture 61 of DeLaViña's "Written on the Wall II" (conjectures of Graffiti.pc): for every finite simple connected graph G on at least two vertices, the number f(G) of vertices of a largest induced forest satisfies f(G) ≥ residue(G) + ⌈diam(G)/3⌉, where residue(G) is the Havel–Hakimi residue of the degree sequence. The formal statement is the one recorded in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture61.lean, theorem `conjecture61`, tagged research open there on 26 November 2026), copied verbatim together with its definitions of the residue and of `largestInducedForestSize`. The proof marks ⌈diam/3⌉ disjoint edges on a diametral geodesic and proves a new lemma: if a vertex set U induces a perfect matching, there is an independent set S outside U with residue(G) ≤ |S| + ⌈|U \ N(S)|/2⌉. The lemma is obtained by a maximum-degree deletion argument with the matching re-paired in deletion order; the classical fact that deleting a maximum-degree vertex does not decrease the residue is proved from the Havel–Hakimi recursion.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 61: f(G) ≥ residue(G) + ⌈diam(G)/3⌉

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization proving Written on the Wall II Conjecture 61: for every nontrivial finite connected simple graph G, the maximum order f(G) of an induced forest satisfies f(G) ≥ residue(G) + ⌈diam(G) / 3⌉, where residue(G) is the Havel-Hakimi residue and diam(G) is the graph diameter. The proof establishes positive maximum-degree vertex-deletion monotonicity for Havel-Hakimi residue from first principles via degree-sequence exchanges and Havel-Hakimi graphicality, proves a matching-residue theorem yielding the general Induced-Matching Residue Inequality R(G) ≤ max(α(G - A), α(G - B)) for every induced matching A ↔ B in any finite simple graph G, applies it to ⌈diam(G) / 3⌉ edges along a diametral geodesic whose sides are 3-packings, and lifts the bound to the exact real-valued statement in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures using only the three standard Lean axioms.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 61: Induced Forest, Residue, and Diameter Bound in Lean 4

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof establishing the sharp additive inequality τ(T) ≤ γ_t(T) + p(T) - 2 for every finite simple tree T on at least two vertices with path cover number p(T) ≥ 2, where τ(T) is the vertex cover number, γ_t(T) is the total domination number, and p(T) is the minimum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint paths covering V(T) (singletons allowed). Because γ_t(T) + p(T) - 2 ≤ γ_t(T) · (p(T) - 1) for all γ_t ≥ 2 and p ≥ 2 (strictly stronger whenever p ≥ 3), this immediately proves all three upstream statements of Written on the Wall II Conjecture 372 in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (conjecture372, variants.two_paths, and variants.regularized). The formal proof uses an original rooted-tree structural induction certified by a kernel-checked finite-state potential table, bridged directly to Mathlib's SimpleGraph.IsTree and SimpleGraph.vertexCoverNum with only the standard axioms.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 372: Sharp Additive Tree Bound in Lean 4

entries.abstract: This project formalizes Theorems 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3 of the supplied V4 manuscript on Turing universality in hypergraph Turán theory. Theorem 1.1 gives a primitive-recursive compiler from binary words to single finite simple three-uniform hypergraphs: ordinary Turán density equals a fixed rational threshold exactly on nonhalting inputs and exceeds it exactly on halting inputs. Theorem 1.2 extends the density dichotomy to finite forbidden families in every uniformity at least three, with joint primitive-recursive compilers, exact density scaling, and input-independent globally optimal templates whose blowups avoid the compiled families. Theorem 1.3 provides a jointly primitive-recursive structural compiler above a fixed rank threshold. Nonhalting inputs have one ordinary extremal profile and edge-edit stability with fixed finite role patterns and exact balanced class sizes. Halting inputs have two disjoint nonempty compact phases, separated by fixed finite test graphs, each homeomorphic to the entire inner extremal space. The package includes the finite computation, obstruction, extremal, suspension, and effective-construction proofs needed for these three results. One independent Challenge and one Comparator configuration select all three theorem declarations.
entries.title: Turing Universality in Hypergraph Turán Theory

entries.abstract: For a finite set A of positive integers let f_A(t) = sum over a in A of cos(2 pi a t), and call D(A) = -min_t f_A(t) the depth of A. Chowla conjectured in 1965 that there is an absolute constant c > 0 such that every nonempty A satisfies min_t f_A(t) < -c sqrt(|A|) (Chowla's cosine problem; Erdős Problem #510). This project is a complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of a counterexample from the manuscript "A prime-square counterexample to Chowla's cosine conjecture" (included as manuscript/chowla_prime_square.pdf): for every eps > 0 there are arbitrarily large finite sets A of positive integers with f_A(t) > -eps sqrt(|A|) for every real t. The manuscript, including the counterexample and its proof, was produced by the AI model Astra 6.2, prompted by Shengtong Zhang. The Lean formalization was then written by Claude Opus 5.5 agents in Cursor. Two theorems are compared. The main one, `Erdos510.erdos_510`, is the negation of the statement of Erdős Problem #510 in Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures repository, copied verbatim from FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/510.lean at commit 7db2ea3 (where it is tagged research open). The second, `cosine_counterexample`, is Theorem 1 of the manuscript, which states exactly the result above. The proof follows the manuscript. A binary profile given by horizontal slices of an annulus is smoothed so that a Fourier multiplier in the logarithm of the radius (computed through the Laplace and Mellin transforms of the Bessel function J_0 and Legendre duplication) produces a family with nonnegative Fourier transform. Auxiliary circle coordinates make the label frequencies primitive integer vectors, a Chinese remainder construction maps them to multiplicatively independent integers, and characters modulo a prime square with an explicit Gauss-sum identity and equidistributed phases realize the required multipliers. Poisson summation over residue classes gives a lower bound for the weighted cosine sum, and the weights are rounded to a set using Spencer's discrepancy theorem, which is proved here from a partial-colouring lemma, together with a discrete de la Vallée-Poussin interpolation bound. The proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: A counterexample to Chowla's cosine conjecture

entries.abstract: In the visible game of cops and robber on a finite connected undirected graph, let c(G) be the least number of cops who can force capture. A multiscale pursuit argument gives c(G) ≤ n^(2/3 + e(n)) on every graph of order n, with one positive function e(n) tending to zero uniformly over the choice of graph. In particular, there are constants δ > 0 and C > 0 such that c(G) ≤ C n^(1 − δ) for every such graph, as asserted by the weak Meyniel conjecture. The repository also contains a separate formalization of the shorter proof giving c(G) ≤ 31 n^(3/4) log(2n).
entries.title: The weak Meyniel conjecture and a two-thirds exponent for the cop number

entries.abstract: With logarithms to base two, let m(n) be the least m for which some n-vertex graph contains both a clique and an independent set of order ⌈log n⌉ in every set of m vertices. In 1991 Erdős asked whether m(n) ≤ ⌈(log n)^3⌉ for arbitrarily large n. We answer this question negatively by proving that m(n) > (log n)^(7/2)/(log log n)^24 for all sufficiently large n, improving a bound of Alon and Sudakov (2007). We also give a simple construction that improves the upper bound of Alon, Bucić and Sudakov (2021) from 2^(2^((log log n)^(1/2+o(1)))) to 2^((9/2+o(1))(log log n)^2). Both bounds are formalized in Lean 4.
entries.title: Improved bounds for locally Ramsey graphs

entries.abstract: Aristotle (De Caelo III.8) claimed that regular tetrahedra fill space; the refutation is credited to Regiomontanus, and the history is told by Lagarias and Zong (2012). This entry proves in Lean that there is no tiling of 3-space by similar copies of the regular tetrahedron, and the same for the regular octahedron, dodecahedron and icosahedron. Tiles are convex polytopes, need not meet face to face, and may each have their own scale. With helper tiles whose dihedral angles are nonnegative rational multiples of pi (cubes, for instance), no tile is a copy of the polyhedron; in a tiling by the five Platonic polyhedra and such helpers, no tile is a dodecahedron or an icosahedron. The proof reads each dihedral angle from the set, uses that the angles round an edge add up to 2 pi (each a dihedral angle, pi or 2 pi), and that pi, arctan of the golden ratio, arccos(1/sqrt 6) and arccos(sqrt(2/3)) are linearly independent over Q, by Niven's theorem (Mathlib niven) and a field argument. Tilings are locally finite by definition, and each polyhedron is one fixed set in exact coordinates. None of these theorems is new; the entry gives their Lean proofs. Audience: researchers on tilings and polyhedra, and Mathlib contributors.
entries.title: Aristotle's Error, Machine-Checked: Regular Tetrahedra Do Not Fill Space

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the paper 'Powers of a Prime in the Image of Summatory Valuation Functions', on the question of Nicolas about the powers of 2 in the image of c(n) = sum_{k=1}^{n} 2^{v_2(k)}. It proves the recurrences and the binary formula for c, the equivalence of Theorem thm:equiv, the greedy lemma, the leading term and the recursion on states with its algorithm, the explicit members and non-members, the one-step classification, the families of Nicolas and their counting, the lower bounds for the counting functions A(x) and B(x) (Theorems thm:counting and thm:counting2), the forest of successful states, the bottom-up recursion and the symmetry, the further families of Theorem thm:symfamilies, and the analogue for an arbitrary prime p (Lemma lem:cp, Proposition prop:Fp, Theorems thm:primes, thm:primestep, thm:primefamilies, thm:immediate, thm:primebottomup and Proposition prop:primezero). Everything is proved from Mathlib. The worked numerical examples of the text and the computations of Section sec:experiments are not formalized.
entries.title: SequenceNicolas: powers of a prime in the image of summatory valuation functions

entries.abstract: In the shifted Antihydra recurrence on natural-number pairs, each successful round sends x to floor(3x/2). Even x earns two units of credit. Odd x spends one unit and halts at zero credit. From (8, 0), no semilinear set containing the seed admits a successful successor within the set for every member. The proof also gives a quantitative horizontal-ray bound and the Presburger-definable corollary. The seed's halting behavior is open in this work, and priority is unclaimed.
entries.title: Antihydra has no semilinear inductive safety invariant

entries.abstract: For every real number ξ > 0, the sequence of integer parts ⌊ξ(7/5)^n⌋, n = 0, 1, 2, …, contains infinitely many composite terms. The Lean proof establishes the stronger statement that infinitely many terms share a nontrivial divisor with 4290 = 2·3·5·11·13, by a finite graph certificate: an orbit avoiding these five primes would give an infinite walk in a finite labelled graph whose vertices record a residue modulo 4290 and a cell of the fractional part, refined in four stages from 32 to 2048 cells, and every cyclic strongly connected component of that graph is excluded by a rank and phase certificate together with an elementary lemma that the carry sequence of such an orbit is not eventually periodic. The finite certificate is checked inside the Lean kernel (`decide +kernel`); no `native_decide` and no axioms beyond `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` are used.
entries.title: Infinitely many composite terms in the floor sequence of ξ(7/5)^n

entries.abstract: A point of the square lattice has eight neighbours. Let delta(n) be the greatest upper density of a set S such that every point of S has at most n neighbours in S. Elkies introduced delta(n) and proved delta(3) = 1/2, which implies that no still Life of Conway's Game of Life has density greater than 1/2 (the still-Life conjecture). Ionascu, Pritikin and Wright studied the limit of the densities of n-dependent sets in finite kings graphs and conjectured the values 3/5 and 9/13 for n = 4 and n = 5, with upper bounds 0.608956 and 0.693943. This project proves delta(3) = 1/2, the same for still Lifes, delta(4) = 3/5 and delta(5) = 9/13, each as the greatest element of the set of upper densities. For n = 3 the proof is the one of Chu and Stuckey. For n = 4 and n = 5 the upper bound is an inequality in windows of four or three rows of five cells with two functions whose contributions telescope; the functions are given by tables, and the kernel checks the inequality in every window. Elkies reports that M. Moore announced delta(5) = 9/13 in 1995. We have not found a published proof for n = 4 or n = 5; whether these two results are new is unknown to us.
entries.title: The greatest density of a set in the square lattice whose points have at most three, four or five neighbours

entries.abstract: DICTO's paper "Fair Dice — The Aequi: Enumerating the Innumerable" (Zenodo, 2026) proves, as its Theorem A (a), that a set of N distinct face directions, not all in one closed hemisphere, carries a die that is fair about the origin (every face seen from the origin under the solid angle 4 pi / N) exactly when the directions satisfy Alexandrov's condition for equal masses, and that the die is then unique up to scale. The proof passes to the polar polytope, whose corners lie on the face directions; the paper's Lemma 1 shows that the solid angle of a face equals the integral Gauss curvature of the polar polytope at the matching corner, so Theorem A (a) is Alexandrov's theorem on prescribed integral curvature (Alexandrov 1942, in the polytope case proved by Oliker 2007 and Bertrand 2016) for equal curvatures. This entry proves in Lean the polyhedral Alexandrov theorem with the condition stated over sets of rays (existence if and only if the curvatures sum to 4 pi and Alexandrov's condition holds for every nonempty proper set of the rays; uniqueness up to scaling about the origin); the equivalence of this form with the textbook form over spherically convex sets is not formalized. Curvature and solid angle are each defined as three times a volume inside the unit ball (the normal cone, or the cone through a face), which equals the corresponding area on the unit sphere. The entry also proves Lemma 1 (the polar identity) and Theorem A (a) (existence and uniqueness of the fair die). Existence follows Oliker's variational route: a maximizer of his functional exists by continuity and coercivity, and at a maximizer every corner has the prescribed curvature. Uniqueness is by the maximum principle. Not formalized: Theorem A (b) (the symmetry group of the die) and (c) (the centre of the die as its centroid; the Lean statements use the origin, and the centroid is not formalized), the finite test for equal masses, and the rest of the paper (the enumeration). Audience: researchers on convex polytopes, the Minkowski and Alexandrov problems and fair dice, and Mathlib contributors.
entries.title: Fair Dice from Curvature: Alexandrov's Theorem, Machine-Checked

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof that a finite simple graph G has a total colouring with Δ(G) + 2 colours (a map on V ⊕ E(G) giving different colours to adjacent vertices, to distinct edges with a common endpoint, and to incident vertex–edge pairs) in three situations: (1) tcc_of_independent: G has an independent set S with |V| ≤ |S| + Δ + 1 (Yap–Wang–Zhang 1989, Lemma 2.2; Yap–Chew 1992, Lemma 2.4); (2) tcc_of_card_le_maxDegree_add_three: Δ(G) ≥ |V| − 3 (Yap–Wang–Zhang 1989, Theorem 2.3 and the closing remarks); (3) tcc_of_card_le_maxDegree_add_four: Δ(G) ≥ |V| − 4, for every finite simple graph (no further hypothesis; Yap–Wang–Zhang 1989, Theorem 2.4). The proofs use Yap's apex-vertex technique: a new vertex joined to the vertices outside one or two independent pairs, matchings found by the enlarge-matching argument (when Δ ≥ 7 or G has three pairwise non-adjacent vertices) or, when G has no three pairwise non-adjacent vertices, the two alternating matchings of a Hamiltonian path through the vertices outside the pairs, and Fournier's theorem (PALOMAR-2026-11-08-000009) or Vizing's theorem (PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000004), both imported as lake dependencies, in place of the Chetwynd–Hilton theorem on three vertices of maximum degree and Kostochka's theorem for Δ ≤ 4 used in the original paper.
entries.title: The total colouring conjecture for graphs of high maximum degree (Yap–Wang–Zhang)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 disproof of Written on the Wall II Conjecture 72 of Graffiti.pc, which asserts tree(G) ≥ ⌈ecc_avg(G) + max_v λ(v)/3⌉ for every finite simple connected graph G, where tree(G) is the order of a largest induced tree, ecc_avg(G) the average eccentricity and λ(v) the independence number of the neighbourhood of v. The counterexample has 19 vertices: two 4-cycles through a common vertex, one of whose far vertices is replaced by a clique of 13 twins. Its eccentricities sum to 70, max_v λ(v) = 4 and tree(G) = 5, so the bound would be ⌈70/19 + 4/3⌉ = 6. The statement is the negation of the Formal Conjectures statement.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 72 is false (a 19-vertex counterexample)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Written on the Wall II Conjecture 372 of Graffiti.pc on its defined domain: every finite tree T on more than two vertices with path cover number p(T) ≥ 2 satisfies γ_t(T) ≥ τ(T) / (p(T) − 1), where γ_t is the total domination number and τ the vertex cover number. Two variants are also proved: τ(T) ≤ γ_t(T) for trees of order at least two that are covered by at most two disjoint paths, and τ(T) ≤ γ_t(T) · max(1, p(T) − 1) for every tree of order at least two. The statements are those of the Formal Conjectures repository.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 372: total domination, vertex covers and path covers of trees

entries.abstract: Formalization of the main results of J. Park's paper on stealthy periodic point configurations with marked cubic period 2Zⁿ. From the 24 sign rows of an order-12 Hadamard matrix and their antipodes it constructs, for n = 10, 11, 12, configurations with stealth radius K = 1 and stealth center density 1/24 that are not translates of lattices (Theorem 1.1). It proves that a motif with K ≥ 1 has at least 2n points, with equality for n ≥ 3 exactly for translated antipodal Hadamard arrays (Theorem 1.2); that K > 1 forces at least 1 + n + n(n−1)/2 points (Lemma 4.1); the exact stealth radius of a binary motif in terms of its dual distance (Proposition 3.1); bounded-complexity and binary optimality of the center density 1/(2n), resp. 1/24, with their equality cases (Theorems 5.1 and 5.3, Corollary 5.2); the strict reciprocal-Gram maximum (Lemma 6.1); and local maximality of the Hadamard configurations under perturbations of the motif and of the marked period, with local isolation for n = 12 (Theorem 1.3, in the marked period model).
entries.title: Hadamard configurations and sharp cubic-period bounds for stealth in dimensions 10, 11, and 12

entries.abstract: This is a formalization of Lebesgue space bounds for higher-dimensional twisted paraproducts in the full open Banach range. This was an open problem in every dimension d >= 2. For d = 2, Kovac (Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 2012, Theorem 1) proved bounds for input exponents 1 < p_1, p_2 < infinity with 1/p_1 + 1/p_2 > 1/2, i.e. target exponents p < 2. For d = 3, Durcik and Roos (Proc. AMS 2021, Sections 1 and 3) proved bounds for 1 < p < 4/3 and 1 < p_i < 4. For d >= 4, no bounds were known for any exponents, as stated in Durcik-Roos (2021, Section 1). The proof and the formalization blueprint were generated with GPT-6.2 Astra Ultra. The formalization was done with GPT-6.2 Sol Light.
entries.title: Boundedness of higher-dimensional twisted paraproducts

entries.abstract:
Complete and unconditional. A Lean 4 formalization of G. Cassese, "A solution to Morrey's problem in R^{2 x m}" (arXiv:2608.03488v3, 2026): rank-one convex integrands on 2 x m matrices, m >= 3, that are nowhere quasiconvex, so that with Šverák's theorem only 2 x 2 remains open; and p-homogeneous examples answering Kirchheim and Kristensen's homogeneous problem negatively.

Every result that the paper proves is proved, with no hypothesis beyond the paper's: Theorem 1.2 (every p > 1, 2 x m for m large, by the paper's UMD route, and a second time by its elementary route), Theorem 1.3 (a quartic on 2 x 3, and p near 4), Corollary 5.3 (its transpose on 3 x 2), the consequences that only 2 x 2 remains, Theorem 1.4 (d x d, every p, and p = 4 for d >= 588), Theorem 1.5 (4 x 2, every p != 2) and Corollary 1.6. The results of other works that the proofs use are proved too, in their sources' terms: Burkholder's inequalities and functions, UMD theory for L^p and the Schatten classes, decoupling, the Kahane-Khintchine and non-commutative Khintchine inequalities, transference for homogeneous multipliers, Dragičević's lower bound for the square of the Beurling-Ahlfors transform, Dacorogna's formula for the quasiconvex envelope, Kristensen's smoothing and the textbook facts of the calculus of variations, by the arguments of their sources (named substitutes stand for a few steps that a source takes from a work that was not read, only recalls, or states without proof: see fidelity). They come from three Lake packages written for this project (lean4-harmonic-analysis, lean4-banach-probability, lean4-calculus-of-variations). The repository formalizes other papers on Morrey's problem too, each its own submission.
entries.title: Cassese 2026: Morrey's problem in R^{2 x m}, in Lean

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalisation, built on mathlib, of L. Niebel, "Lions' Maximal Regularity Problem for Divergence-Form Differential Operators: Failure at the 1/2-Hölder Endpoint" (arXiv:2608.11194v2), an arXiv preprint. J.-L. Lions asked whether the variational solution of u' + A(t)u = f, u(0) = 0, with forms of bounded measurable coefficients, has maximal L^2-regularity, u' in L^2(0,T;H), when f is in L^2(0,T;H). The paper shows that 1/2-Hölder continuity in time with values in L^infinity does not suffice: on the interval (0,pi) it constructs a bounded, uniformly elliptic, real scalar coefficient, 1/2-Hölder continuous in time with values in L^infinity(0,pi) and arbitrarily close to 1, a continuous L^2-valued forcing, and the unique Lions variational solution, whose time derivative is not square integrable (Theorem 1.1); and, by zero extension, tensorisation and parabolic rescaling, real symmetric isotropic counterexamples on R^d and on every bounded domain of R^d, d >= 1 (Corollary 1.2). The compared theorems are Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, stated in Challenge.lean in the paper's spaces H = L^2, V = H^1_0 (the closure of the graphs of C^1_c functions) and V' (its anti-dual), with uniqueness of the Lions solution. The repository formalises, in its own terms and with every deviation recorded in DEVIATIONS.md, the other numbered statements of the paper, one of them in part (Corollary 7.1 directly, without the cited sufficiency theorems and the operator-theoretic side conditions), with no counterpart for Remark 3.1 (a comment without a claim), and proves Lions' uniqueness theorem in the paper's complex spaces; about 21,000 lines of Lean in 61 library modules; every theorem of the library depends only on the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and there is no sorry outside the two deliberate ones in Challenge.lean.
entries.title: Lions' maximal regularity problem for divergence-form differential operators: failure at the 1/2-Hölder endpoint

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of the density Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem: uniform finite integral extremal density, weighted and graphon density, the complete B/A/R equality classification including every transition and endpoint, uniform finite and graphon stability with its corollaries, and perfect rainbow clique factors. Palomar mechanically verified commit a5920fc397ac727bc603bbd027cb8b4d700c98b6 in run 45581673183 on 2026-11-25.
entries.title: Density Hajnal–Szemerédi formalization

entries.abstract:
An infinite Ammann–Beenker network is a mathematical graph with octagonal geometry. In this particular network, two localized wave patterns share a special energy, as established in [PALOMAR-2026-11-06-000012 (version 1)](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-06-000012&version=1). [PALOMAR-2026-11-23-000017 (version 1)](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-23-000017&version=1) describes how changing a single edge splits their energy. [PALOMAR-2026-11-25-000001 (version 1)](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-25-000001&version=1) shows how two coordinated controls can prepare any normalized mixture of the two patterns, up to a common phase, without leakage. The present theorem asks whether their energies can also remain separated from all the other energies while those controls are active.

The first control changes a common onsite parameter on eight first-ring vertices by a signed amount δ. The second changes eight distinct inter-ring edges, with no shared endpoints, by a signed amount η. The two localized patterns span a space that both controls preserve exactly. Its two energy levels have midpoint E* + δ/2 + η, where E* is their original common energy, and half-spacing s = √(δ²/4 + η²). Both levels have genuine nonzero eigenvectors of the full infinite operator; they coincide only when both controls vanish. The orthogonal complement is also preserved on the natural operator domain.

At zero control, the certified gap around E* is 1/128. Write ρ = |δ| + 2|η| for the combined control size. The new theorem proves that if ρ/2 + s is less than 1/128, the complete real spectrum contains exactly the two controlled energies in the closed interval between them. Each is separated from every other real spectral energy by at least 1/128 − ρ/2 − s, which is strictly positive. Every eigenvector at either controlled energy lies entirely in the original localized space. The case of coincident energies at zero control is included.

Since s is at most ρ/2, the simpler condition ρ < 1/128 also guarantees protection, with separation at least 1/128 − ρ. This includes either control acting alone, with |δ| < 1/128 or |η| < 1/256, respectively. These bounds are sufficient, not claimed optimal.

The result is proved in Lean for the full infinite operator with its confining potential and natural domain, not for a finite sample or a two-state approximation. It adds a quantitative energy gap to exact geometric decoupling. It provides a foundation for studying imperfect controls, but does not prove noise tolerance, arbitrary-strength protection, experimental feasibility or general quantum dynamics.
entries.title: Spectral Protection During Coordinated Control on an Infinite Ammann–Beenker Graph

entries.abstract: Let b(n, l) be the number of parking functions of length n whose maximum displacement is exactly l, where the displacement of a car is the distance between the spot it takes and its preferred spot, and call the sequence b(n, 0), b(n, 1), ..., b(n, n-1) row n. The formalization proves two theorems in Lean 4 with Mathlib. The first, the staircase (Parking.staircase), says that for every n >= 2 there is a position p such that row n rises strictly up to b(n, p), satisfies b(n, p+1) <= b(n, p), and falls strictly from b(n, p+1) on, and such that row n+1 either has the same shape with the same p or rises strictly up to b(n+1, p+1) and falls strictly after it. So every row is strictly increasing and then strictly decreasing, except that the entry directly after the peak may be equal to the peak, and the peak stays or moves one position to the right when the length grows by one. The second (Parking.unimodal_via_staircase) is the corollary that for every n >= 1 row n is unimodal, which is Conjecture 6.5 of Celano, Elder, Hadaway, Harris, Martin, Priestley and Udell (arXiv:2507.07243). The numbers b(n, l) are defined directly from the parking process. The staircase is obtained by induction on n from two rules for the sign of the step b(n, k) - b(n, k-1): a positive step stays positive one row down in the same column, and a step that is not positive is followed by a negative step one row down and one column to the right. The rules are proved region by region: tables that Lean's kernel evaluates in exact integer arithmetic settle the small columns, and analytic estimates settle the large ones. The proof depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The unimodality had been proved before, by another route, in the formalization MegasKomnenos/parking-unimodality (PALOMAR-2026-11-25-000002), on whose library this proof is built. As far as a literature search found, the staircase is first presented by this formalization and the package from which it was made; that it is new is not established. The proof was found, written and formalized by AI sessions. A person has read the two Lean statements, with the definitions they use, against the statements in words; no person has refereed the mathematics.
entries.title: The staircase theorem for parking functions counted by maximum displacement

entries.abstract: A Mathlib-only Lean 4 formalization of the manuscript Characterizations of E-finite algebras and conjectures on brick-finiteness by Haruhisa Enomoto. A finite-dimensional algebra over a field is E-finite when its two-term silting fan covers the integral projective lattice K₀(proj Λ). Theorem A proves that E-finiteness is equivalent over an arbitrary field to seventeen conditions—including nonzero morphisms between nonzero modules of equal dimension vector (K₀-Hom), injectivity of dimension-vector maps on torsion-class Grothendieck monoids, functorial finiteness of compact torsion classes and wide subcategories, finiteness of semibricks, finiteness of bricks of each endolength, polynomial brick growth, absence of generic bricks and generic grains, presilting generation of two-term thick subcategories, and finite-dimensionality of universal localizations and simple Artinian epimorphic targets—together with two dimension-vector finiteness conditions over infinite fields and three geometric conditions (King moduli closed points, open brick orbits, and open wide loci) over algebraically closed fields. Consequently, seven open brick-finiteness conjectures (including Demonet's lattice point conjecture, the finite semibrick conjecture, the second brick-Brauer–Thrall conjecture, and Mousavand–Paquette's generic brick conjecture) become equivalent for each algebra. Theorem B proves this common conjecture in rank at most two over any field, equating E-finiteness, brick-finiteness, and τ-tilting finiteness. Corollary C proves Weyman's conjecture over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic, equating Schur-representation-finiteness with multiplicity-freeness on every irreducible component. Intended for researchers in the representation theory of finite-dimensional algebras, silting and τ-tilting theory, and module varieties.
entries.title: Characterizations of E-finite algebras and conjectures on brick-finiteness

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of the Eastin-Knill theorem: a quantum code of dimension at least two that detects every error on a single subsystem has no universal set of transversal logical gates. The system has finitely many sites of any finite dimensions; a code is an orthogonal projector P; it detects single-site errors when P E P is a multiple of P for every operator E on one site; a transversal gate is a tensor product of one unitary per site, and it is logical when it commutes with P. Up to a scalar on the code there are only finitely many logical transversal gates; if the code has dimension at least two they are not universal, since some logical unitary differs on the code by a fixed distance from every logical transversal gate times every scalar. The same holds for transversal gates across several code blocks (Eastin and Knill's Corollary 1). The proof avoids Lie theory: near the identity a transversal gate is exp(i H) with H a sum of single-site operators, error detection makes it act on the code as a scalar, so the gates acting as scalars form an open subgroup of a compact group, which has finite index. A three-qutrit code is constructed to show the hypotheses can be met.
entries.title: The Eastin-Knill theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the main results of Fan, Stone, Yang and Yin, "Localization-delocalization transition for a random block matrix model" (arXiv:2504.00512). The model is H_Lambda = H + Lambda, complex Hermitian case: H has D >= 2 independent N x N Wigner blocks on the diagonal, with entry laws whose moments are bounded by given constants (Assumption 1), and Lambda places a deterministic A and A* on the cyclic off-diagonal blocks. This entry contains Theorem 2.1 (delocalized regime: under ||A|| <= N^{-delta_A} and (2.4), every eigenvector puts mass 1/D + O(N^{-c}) on each block, (2.5)) and Theorem 2.5 (localized regime: the eigenvalue shift bounds (2.10), (2.11) and the comparison of the local correlation functions with those of H). Both are stated in uniform form (constants chosen before N, then every N >= N_0, every entry law with the given moment constants, every admissible A and every k) and have no hypotheses other than their parameters; no result of another work is assumed for them. The library also proves Theorem 2.2 and Theorem 2.4, each from one external input stated as an explicit hypothesis; those two are not part of this entry.
entries.title: Localization-delocalization transition for a random block matrix model

entries.abstract: There is a countable group that is hyperlinear and not sofic. This answers in the negative Open question 3.4 of Pestov's guide to hyperlinear and sofic groups (2008): "Is every hyperlinear group sofic?" Soficity and hyperlinearity are stated through finite models: maps to the permutations of a finite set, respectively to unitary matrices, that are multiplicative on a given finite set up to epsilon and separate its elements by 1 - epsilon in normalized Hamming distance, respectively by 2 - epsilon in squared normalized Hilbert-Schmidt distance. The development proves that the first notion is equivalent to the criterion of Pestov's Theorem 3.5 and that the second implies the criterion of his Theorem 3.6. The group is the quotient of GL_3(A) x| St by the subgroup generated by a central element of infinite order, where A is a ring that is free of rank 8 over Z[1/2] with a nilpotent ideal of rank 7, and St is the stabilizer of a vector in GL_3(Z[1/2]). Hyperlinearity of such a central quotient is an instance of a theorem of Thom (2010) and is proved here directly. The non-soficity is the new part: the image of EL_3(A) has Kazhdan's property (T), and eight elements normalizing it act on three of its central elements in a way that no sofic approximation can follow. The proof reuses the Lean developments of OpenAI (Kun's theorem on sofic approximations of Kazhdan groups, cluster groups) and of the group-approximation project (the theorem of Ershov and Jaikin-Zapirain). This formalization does not certify finite generation or finite presentation of the group, the equivalence of the local criteria with the ultraproduct definitions, or anything about other groups.
entries.title: A countable group that is hyperlinear and not sofic

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1.1 of van den Brand, Chen, Kyng, Liu, Peng, Probst Gutenberg, Sachdeva and Sidford: there is a deterministic algorithm that, given a graph with m edges, integral demands and capacities bounded by U and integral costs bounded by C, computes an exact minimum-cost flow in time m^(1+o(1)) log U log C. The algorithm is one program for a word RAM, and the proof shows that on every well-formed instance it halts with a correct answer within K*n + (m+2)^(1+eps(m)) * log(U+2) * log(C+2) steps, with eps(m) tending to 0. Every cited result that the paper uses is proved in the library, or replaced by a proof of the step that uses it.
entries.title: Deterministic almost-linear-time minimum-cost flow

entries.abstract: Lean 4 (v4.35.0) + Mathlib formalization of the base-b last-digit Collatz family f_b(n) = n/2 (even n) and (n mod b)*n + 1 (odd n), focusing on the base-10 Ouroboros map f = f_10 and stating the open OuroborosConjecture definition alongside 38 unconditionally proved compared theorems (zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only). Collectively, the 38 theorems establish six principal result families: (1) small-base resolutions, including base-4 equivalence to the classical 3x+1 Collatz conjecture and global convergence to 1 in bases 2 and 5; (2) base-10 exponential Terras stopping-time descent (p_k <= 1.124953 * 0.996423^k) and density-one descent, together with a complete all-even-base stopping-time dichotomy (p_infty(b) = 0 iff b in {2, 4, 6, 10}) and even-base drift classification; (3) the base-10 basin-of-1 modulo-30 residue law, exact 2-adic Cantor closure and ultrametric isometry, and exact Hausdorff and box-counting dimension dim_H = dim_B = beta = -log_2 a (plus congruence-class completions and exact base-b suffix-closure dimension in every base b >= 2); (4) sharp pure-kernel basin growth bounds (0.0145 X^(399/800) <= N_1(X) <= C X^0.6245 with limsup (log N_1 / log X) <= 0.6245 < beta, N_5(X) > 0.02134 X^(13/20), and strict separation N_1(X)/N_5(X) <= C X^(-0.0255) -> 0); (5) universal odd-base Markov absorption for all odd b >= 3 and a certified 905/999 odd-base survey through b <= 1999 (27 trap-only and 878 split rational densities, plus explicit b = 3, 5, 7, 13 evaluations); and (6) base-10 cycle obstructions (digit-cancellation, halving-budget, K > 64000 tail, and unconditional classification of all cycles with m <= 3 odd members alongside the two known cycles through 1 and 5). Main results in the companion paper: 15 of 16 proved main results in Lean 4 (94%) · 1 of 16 by external computation (exhaustive sweep and cycle lower bounds through 10^15) · 0 by written proof · Global conjecture open. Within this package, 19 library modules in Ouroboros/ (plus Challenge.lean and Solution.lean) import Mathlib directly while the 104 finite certificate shards (BasinFiveCert*, EvenBasesCert, BasinOneLowerCert*, BasinOneUpperCert*, and OddSurveyCert*) verify finite integer inequalities by Init-only kernel reduction (rfl). Companion working paper, exact external checkers, and logged prior-work searches are published at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/the-ouroboros-conjecture.html.
entries.title: The Ouroboros Conjecture: Competing Attractors in Base 10 Among Last-Digit Collatz Maps

entries.abstract: DICTO's paper "From Dehn Packets to Scutoids: How the Fullerene Star Fills Space" (Zenodo, 2026) proves, as its Theorem 4, that two pairs of icosahedral pieces whose Dehn invariants cancel cannot tile space: (a) no tiling of 3-space contains a dodecahedron centre pyramid or a truncated icosahedron if every tile is a similar copy (motion, reflection, positive scaling) of one of these two, of the dodecahedron, the icosahedron, the truncated octahedron or the truncated cuboctahedron, or a convex polytope whose dihedral angles are all nonnegative rational multiples of pi; (b) the same for the icosahedron centre pyramid and the truncated dodecahedron. The tiling need not be face to face. This entry proves (a) and (b) in Lean, with each named solid given by exact face inequalities over Q(sqrt 5) or Q(sqrt 2) and its dihedral angles read from the set itself, as in the registered Dehn Canon entry: at an edge point, the share of a small disc across the edge that lies in the tangent cone. It also proves the paper's two lemmas: Lemma 3, that pi, arctan(phi), arccos(1/sqrt 6) and arccos(sqrt(2/3)) are linearly independent over Q (Niven's theorem in Mathlib and a field argument), and Lemma 2 in the weaker form the proof of Theorem 4 needs: at an edge point x of a tile of a tiling by convex polytopes (locally finite, not necessarily face to face) there are finitely many tiles with numbers summing to 2 pi, the given tile's being its angle at x and each other being pi, 2 pi, or a dihedral angle of that tile read at some edge point of it, chosen independently and not necessarily on the given edge. The paper takes Lemma 2 from DICTO's earlier paper "Aristotle's Pyramid"; it is the edge-counting step behind Debrunner's theorem (1980). The proof of Theorem 4 counts the angles round one edge: the coefficients of the three irrational angles must cancel within one turn, and a weight argument removes the pieces one after another. All the paper's helpers are covered, the truncated icosidodecahedron included, each built from exact coordinates. Not formalized in the Challenge: Theorem 4 (c), on the smallest ring, is proved in the library but is not in the Challenge; the rest of the paper (scutoid fillings, the Fullerene Star). Audience: researchers on tilings, space-filling polyhedra and scissors congruence, and Mathlib contributors.
entries.title: Dehn Packets in Lean: two icosahedral pairs that cannot fill space

entries.abstract: Lean 4 (v4.35.0) + Mathlib formalization of structural theorems, edge-dual linear-programming relaxations (Lemma W and refinements), Lemma C, local obstruction rules, unconditional counterexample lower bounds, explicit ceiling witnesses, and conditional transfer theorems for Giuga's conjecture (1950). Across 21 compared theorems (zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only), Lean 4 proves unconditionally that every Giuga counterexample has at least 578 distinct prime factors and exceeds 10^1803 (at least 1,804 decimal digits), constructs an explicit 8,135-prime normal odd prime set (40,733 digits) and an explicit 8,138-prime witness satisfying all seven local counterexample rules (40,751 digits), proves all forms of Lemma W, Lemma C, and the mod-8 count congruence, and proves conditional lifting theorems reaching >= 8,138 prime factors and > 10^40747 (>= 40,748 decimal digits) from explicit depth-6 frontier hypotheses. Main results in the companion paper: 0 of 2 headline theorems purely in Lean 4 (0%) · 2 of 2 by Lean 4 + external exact-integer certificates (all 15 prefixes below 17). Existence of a Giuga counterexample remains open. Companion working paper, exact integer checker, and prior-work search log: https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/giuga.
entries.title: How Many Prime Factors Could a Counterexample to Giuga's Conjecture Have?

entries.abstract: At every sufficiently large order n, we construct a split graph with an integral–fractional clique-partition gap of order at least (pn)^(3/2). If p^2 n exceeds an explicit constant times log n, independent survival of crossing edges with probability p leaves, with probability at least 1 - 2 n^(-8), both a complete physical reassignment and the same gap. The accompanying bipartite lemma explicitly chooses each host from its own surviving list.
entries.title: Physical host recovery and gap preservation after random crossing-edge deletions

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of maximum flows and shortest paths. Plane graphs are combinatorial maps (darts with a reversal, a tail vertex, a face and a next dart along the face boundary) whose graph and dual are connected and which satisfy Euler's formula |V| + |F| = |D|/2 + 2. The machine statements are about one explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, natural registers and memory cells bounded by a word bound W along the run) and fixed encodings of the inputs as lists of natural numbers; each asserts one fixed word program for all inputs (the machine also has exact real registers, and a word program contains no instruction that uses them). Six theorems are compared: (1) the max-flow min-cut theorem for a network with nonnegative integer capacities and disjoint sets of sources and sinks: some flow and some cut have equal value and capacity, so the flow is maximum and the cut minimum; (2) the theorem of Miller and Naor: on a plane map, given an antisymmetric g with net outflow b at every vertex, a b-flow within the capacities u exists if and only if the dual graph with lengths u - g has a feasible potential; (3) a word program decides, for every well-formed encoding of a plane map with V vertices, F faces and S darts, natural capacities, supplies and demands, whether a feasible flow exists, within 26 (S + 2)(V + F + 2) steps; (4) a word program prints, for each vertex of a digraph with n vertices, m arcs and natural lengths, its distance from a source capped at a given value INF (so INF for unreachable vertices), within (n + m + 1)(36 floor(log2 n) + 143) steps; (5) a word program prints the size of a maximum matching of a bipartite graph with n vertices and m arcs within 80 (n + 1)(n + m + 1) steps; (6) there are a word program and constants c and k such that, for every well-formed encoding of a plane map (loops allowed) with n darts, K vertices, natural capacities and disjoint sets of sources and sinks, and every word bound W >= c (7 s)^k, where s is n + K plus the total capacity plus 2, the program prints a maximum flow from the sources to the sinks, as a table of flow values together with a valid index into it for every dart, within c (n + K + 1)(floor(log2 n) + 1)^3 steps; this is the algorithm of Borradaile, Klein, Mozes, Nussbaum and Wulff-Nilsen. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Flows and shortest paths in plane graphs, with machine programs including the maximum-flow algorithm of Borradaile, Klein, Mozes, Nussbaum and Wulff-Nilsen, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Zero-Mathlib Lean 4.35.0 formalization resolving two structural questions left open by Vinciguerra's operator analysis of passive-output catalytic register programs (arXiv:2609.18692). The 17 compared theorems prove: (1) an exact base-p digit-sum dichotomy f in RP^{pass}_{F_p}(2, t) iff s_p(d) <= min(p - 1, t - 1) for all d >= 2 with alpha_d != 0, yielding unbounded-degree 2-access Frobenius collapse (x^{p^m}), exact F_2 saturation (x^3 impossible for all t), the impossibility threshold s_p(d) >= p, characteristic-0 recovery for d < p, and a literal commutative-ring soundness bridge; (2) strictly bilinear 2-access Frobenius collapse x^{2^k} in k + 1 registers and 4k - 2 bilinear ops over any characteristic-2 commutative ring; (3) explicit 3-register Pascal-row shear loops computing x^7, x^9, x^11, x^13, and x^15 in 5..9 accesses, unconditional global integer optimality of log_13 8 < 30/37 < log_{2t-3} t for all t >= 4 (t != 8), complete 4-register passive powering for every N >= 1 in < (104/3) * 8^ell accesses, and pointwise product-ring streaming frequency moments F_D over R^n; and (4) a balanced zero-workspace bilinear multilinear product x_0...x_{2^k - 1} with every operation explicitly constrained by CatOp.usesOnly to at most k + 2 designated registers and exact primitive op count (7 * (2^k)^2 - 4) / 3.
entries.title: Positive-Characteristic Dichotomy and Optimal Three-Register Exponents in Passive Catalytic Register Programs

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of sensitivity-versus-real-degree bounds for Boolean functions f : {0, 1}^n -> {0, 1}, motivated by Terence Tao's Optimization Constant #37a. Establishes exact real polynomial degree via Boolean-lattice Mobius inversion, explicit kernel-verified witnesses (3, 2, 3), (6, 3, 6), (9, 4, 9), and (13, 5, 13), the asymptotic lower bound log 6 / log 3 <= degSensitivityExponent via iterated composition and the Chebyshev cubic upper bound, exact sharp bounds B_2 = 3, B_3 = 6, a zero-search 10-line elementary algebraic proof of B_4 = 9, and sharpened low-degree upper bounds B_5 <= 14, B_6 <= 20, B_7 <= 28, B_8 <= 36, and B_9 <= 46 strictly improving the univariate symmetrisation LP bounds of Wellens (2022) via pure-integer Terwilliger LP/PSD certificates, sum-of-squares rigidity, and forbidden-subgraph arguments. These fixed-degree bounds do not alter the known bounds [log_3 6, 2] on either the asymptotic uniform-big-O exponent `degSensitivityExponent` or Tao's distinct finite-supremum constant `C_37`.
entries.title: DegreeSensitivity: Sharp Low-Degree Sensitivity Bounds for Boolean Functions

entries.abstract:
A string rewriting system is a finite set of rules l -> r between words. Its derivation graph has the words as vertices and the rewriting steps x l y -> x r y as edges. This entry proves in Lean 4 and Mathlib Squier's theorem: for a terminating system, one resolution cell per critical pair generates every homotopy between parallel zig-zag paths of derivations. Hence a finite convergent system over a finite alphabet has finite derivation type (Squier, Otto and Kobayashi 1994). Nine statements are compared.
Homotopy modulo a set B of 2-cells (pairs of parallel paths) is the smallest relation on parallel paths that contains B and the independence squares (two steps rewriting disjoint factors commute), identifies a step followed by its inverse, in either order, with the empty path, is an equivalence relation, and is compatible with concatenation, inversion and whiskering by contexts x _ y. B is a homotopy basis if any two parallel paths are homotopic modulo B. A system has finite derivation type if it has a finite homotopy basis. A critical branching is a pair of distinct, non-independent steps from a common word with minimal context, that is, an overlap or an inclusion of two left-hand sides.
(1) Newman's lemma for an arbitrary relation: terminating and locally confluent implies confluent. (2) The critical pair lemma for string rewriting: a system is locally confluent if and only if every critical branching is joinable. (3) Hence a terminating system is confluent if and only if its critical branchings are joinable. (4) Over a finite alphabet, a finite system has finitely many critical branchings. (5) Squier's theorem in homotopy-basis form: for a terminating system, every set of cells containing, for each critical branching, a cell formed by the branching and some resolution of it (in either orientation) is a homotopy basis. The resolutions are arbitrary, so every choice of one resolution per critical pair gives a homotopy basis. (6) Squier's theorem: a finite convergent system over a finite alphabet has finite derivation type. (7) Non-degeneracy: the homotopy relation does not identify everything. For the system aa -> e, bb -> e, bab -> aba and no cells, the two one-step rewrites aaa -> a are not homotopic, which a parity-weighted count of aa-steps detects. (8)-(9) That system, a complete presentation of the symmetric group S3 = <a, b | a^2 = b^2 = 1, bab = aba>, is terminating and confluent, and its five explicit critical-pair cells form a homotopy basis.
The proof of (5) follows Squier and Guiraud–Malbos. Normal-form paths are chosen by well-founded recursion. A noetherian induction then shows that every step followed by the normal-form path of its target is homotopic to the normal-form path of its source, resolving each local branching as an independence square, a trivial branching, or a whiskered critical cell. All results are classical. We searched for a previous machine-checked proof of Squier's theorem (November 2026) and found none; priority among formalizations is nevertheless unknown.
entries.title: Squier's theorem: finite convergent string rewriting systems have finite derivation type, with Newman's lemma, the critical pair lemma and the symmetric group S3 as a worked example

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the three main theorems of the paper "Prescribed holes in the time frequency plane and ptychographic phase retrieval" by J. de Dios Pont, P. Jaming, L. Liehr and M. A. Taylor. (1) Every nonzero window in L²(ℝᵈ) whose ambiguity function has a bounded open zero set does phase retrieval. (2) Every bounded regular open subset of ℝ²ᵈ is, after a sufficiently small rescaling and a translation away from the origin, together with its reflection the open zero set of an ambiguity function. (3) There is an annulus centered at the origin of ℝ² that is not contained in the open zero set of the ambiguity function of any nonzero function in L²(ℝ).
entries.title: Prescribed holes in the time frequency plane and ptychographic phase retrieval

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the domination inequality (Lemma dom of P. Keevash, "The existence of designs II", arXiv:1802.05900, recalled there from "The existence of designs", Lemma 2.4; a form of Freedman's inequality) for random variables on a finite product of independent uniformly random permutations. All statements are exact finite inequalities on the space of all tuples (ω_c)_{c∈ι} of permutations ω_c of [a_c], ι finite, with the uniform measure. (1) DesignsII.freedman_perm: let F be a real function of the tuple, b_c ≥ 0 with b_c ≤ C (C > 0) such that changing the coordinate c changes F by at most b_c, and m_c such that for each c either b_c ≤ m_c, or F depends on ω_c only through an event E_c ⊆ Perm([a_c]) and 2·P(E_c)·b_c ≤ m_c; if ∑_c m_c > 0, then for every λ > 0, P(F − E F ≥ λ) ≤ exp(−λ²/(2C(λ + ∑_c m_c))). (2) DesignsII.count_tail_perm: for a counting variable X = #{β ∈ D : Ev_β}, if each event Ev_β (β ∈ D) is unaffected by the coordinates c with β ∉ Inf_c, |D ∩ Inf_c| ≤ C for every c, and for each c either |D ∩ Inf_c| ≤ m_c or the events Ev_β (β ∈ D ∩ Inf_c) depend on ω_c only through an event E_c with 2·P(E_c)·|D ∩ Inf_c| ≤ m_c, then, if ∑_c m_c > 0, for every λ > 0, P(|X − E X| ≥ λ) ≤ 2·exp(−λ²/(2C(λ + ∑_c m_c))). The point of these variance-sensitive bounds, as opposed to the bounded-differences inequality (Lemma lip3 of the paper, which gives P(|X − E X| > t) ≤ 2exp(−t²/(2B)) with B = ∑_c a_c b_c²), is that a coordinate whose change can move X by a large amount b_c, but only with small probability, contributes 2·P(E_c)·b_c instead of a_c·b_c² to the variance proxy; in the nibble of the paper (Lemma 3.9) the degree of an atom is a count of copies whose activation coordinates have exactly this form, and the bounded-differences bound is too weak there when q − r ≥ 2. Mathlib does not contain these results.
entries.title: Keevash, The existence of designs II: Lemma dom (Freedman's inequality) for independent uniform permutations

entries.abstract: Theorem 1.1 of C. David, A. Dunn, A. Hamieh and H. Lin (arXiv:2306.11875) bounds the sums of normalized quartic Gauss sums g(c) over primary primes c of Z[i] in a class modulo 4, twisted by (c/|c|)^l. The companion note extends it to g(nu, c) with any fixed numerator nu. The only new ingredient is a local identity that splits off the primes dividing nu from the coprimality conditions of the Type I Dirichlet series. This development formalizes that step from the identities of DDHL Section 3, taken as hypotheses on an abstract symbol and Gauss sum: the splitting identity g(mu, pi^k c') = (-1)^C(c', pi^k) g(mu, pi^k) g(mu pi^(2k), c') with no condition linking mu and pi, and DDHL (3.6). It proves the identity for the truncated series as an exact finite identity (Lemma 2.2), and removes pi from the coprimality condition for every valuation e = ord_pi(mu) (Corollary 2.3): on the series prime to pi the valuation reduces modulo 4; for every e the splitting has the terms k = 4j <= e and k = e + 1; and for the four exact valuations e = 1, 3 it gives single equations with an explicit finite inverse, for e = 0, 2 the coupled pair of DDHL (8.6)-(8.7). It also proves lower bounds for the determinants on Re s >= 1 and the 2-adic facts behind the signs.
entries.title: FixedNumerator: the local step in extending a theorem on quartic Gauss sums over primes to a fixed numerator

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalization of V. Šverák, "Rank-one convexity does not imply quasiconvexity", Proc. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh Sect. A 120 (1992), 185-189: a quartic polynomial F on 3x2 matrices that is rank-one convex but not quasiconvex, and its lift to m x n matrices for m >= 3 and n >= 2, which answers Morrey's problem negatively for maps with at least three components.

Every result of the paper is proved by the paper's argument: Lemma 1 (quasiconvexity of a continuous function is tested by periodic maps), the structure of the subspace L and the computation (4), Lemma 2 (the extension of f from L to a rank-one convex F), the Theorem, the Remark (F is a polynomial of degree four) and the Corollary. Nothing is assumed, and the proofs use only Mathlib. The repository formalizes other papers on Morrey's problem too, each its own submission.
entries.title: Šverák 1992: rank-one convexity does not imply quasiconvexity, in Lean

entries.abstract:
A formalization of A. Agazzi et al., Sharp higher integrability theory, Part I: the L^p-norm of the Beurling–Ahlfors transform (arXiv:2609.28311v2). With A z = a₊ z + a₋ z̄, the integrand L (A) = |a₊|² − |a₋|² for |a₊| + |a₋| ≤ 1 and 2|a₊| − 1 otherwise is quasiconvex on R^{2×2}: the integral over the torus of L (A + Dφ) − L (A) is nonnegative for every matrix A and every smooth (in fact every Lipschitz) periodic map φ (Theorem 1).

Hence (Corollary 2) the Burkholder integrands B_p are quasiconvex for every 1 < p < ∞, and the norm of the Beurling–Ahlfors transform on L^p(C) is p* − 1, p* = max (p, p/(p − 1)): Iwaniec's conjecture of 1982. Also proved: the Hessian case of Theorem 1, the uniqueness of the projection in Lemma 4, and Astala's sharp higher integrability of quasiconformal maps as a consequence of Corollary 2, with its sharpness. The cited results that the paper uses are proved too (Kinderlehrer–Stampacchia, Baernstein–Montgomery-Smith, Guerra, Lehto); the results it cites only for context, such as the earlier upper bounds for the norm and the earlier quasiconvexity results, are not formalized.
entries.title: Iwaniec's conjecture: the quasiconvexity of L and the L^p norm of the Beurling–Ahlfors transform (Agazzi et al., arXiv:2609.28311)

entries.abstract: For a prime p and 0 < h < p, the Dedekind sum s(h,p) is determined, up to an explicit error of order log p, by the fractions of small height congruent to plus or minus h: with the sum over the coprime pairs u, v >= 1 with uv < p/2, |12 s(h,p) - p sum ([hv = u mod p] - [hv = -u mod p])/(uv)| <= 6n <= 12 log_2 p + 6, where n is the length of Euclid's algorithm on (p, h). Summed over any set H of residues, in particular over a subgroup of odd order, this gives |12 sum_{h in H} s(h,p) - p S_H(p)| <= |H| (12 log_2 p + 6), where S_H(p) is the signed sum of 1/(uv) over the coprime pairs with uv < p/2 and u/v in H or -H. The development proves Dedekind reciprocity from scratch (by counting lattice points), the identities of Euclid's algorithm and the bound n <= 2 log_2 k + 1, the alternating-sum form 12 s(h,k) = sum (-1)^{j+1} k/(r_j q_{j-1}) + E with |E| <= 4n, and Legendre's pairing of the small coprime pairs with the steps of the algorithm, by a lattice-basis argument instead of continued fractions.
entries.title: SmallRatio: Dedekind sums along Euclid's algorithm and the small-ratio formula

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 (v4.35.0) + Mathlib formalization establishing exact values of the balanced-sequence repetition threshold RTB(d) for alphabets of size 7, 9, and 10: RTB(7) = RTB*(7) = 6/5 < 5/4, RTB(9) = RTB*(9) = 8/7 < 7/6, and RTB(10) = RTB*(10) = 9/8 < 8/7, refuting three of the six values (d - 2)/(d - 3) listed as established for 5 <= d <= 10 in papers from 2018 to 2023. Each infimum is proved both from below via an exhaustive finite prefix-refutation witness tree checked by kernel reduction (905, 2941, and 4868 nodes respectively) and from above via an explicit 1-balanced Sturmian-colouring witness (v7, v9, v10) using all d letters and attaining its critical exponent as a maximum over minimal-period factors. Main results in the companion paper: 6 of 6 in Lean 4 (100%) · 12 of 12 abstract claims in Lean 4 (100%) · 18 of 18 paper claims in Lean 4 (100%) · 0 by external certificate · 0 by written proof. Within BalancedRepetitionThreshold, 11 of 13 Lean files import Mathlib; all 26 compared theorems in Solution.lean and all 193 public theorems in BalancedRepetitionThreshold compile with zero sorry, zero native_decide, and Lean's standard axioms only. The cases d = 5, 6, 8, and d >= 11 are not addressed. Companion working paper and verification archives are hosted at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/balanced-sequences-critical-exponent.
entries.title: Balanced-Sequence Repetition Threshold Refutation: Exact RTB(7) = 6/5, RTB(9) = 8/7, and RTB(10) = 9/8

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the main results of Dubova, Yang, Yau and Yin, "Delocalization of non-mean-field random matrices in dimensions d >= 3" (arXiv:2507.20274). The model is the Gaussian block band matrix on the torus Z_{WL}^d with L^d blocks of size W^d, N = (WL)^d, with the variance profile (2.5) under the size conditions (2.9), (2.10). For every dimension d >= 3, this entry contains Theorem 2.1 (delocalization of the bulk eigenvectors), Theorem 2.2 (the local law, (2.14)-(2.15)), Theorem 2.3 (quantum unique ergodicity, (2.18)-(2.19)) and Theorem 2.5 (quantum diffusion, (2.22)-(2.25)); they have no hypotheses other than their parameters, and no result of another work is assumed for them. The library also proves Theorem 2.4 (bulk universality) and Theorem 2.7 (the block Anderson model) from one external input, stated as an explicit hypothesis; those two are not part of this entry.
entries.title: Delocalization of non-mean-field random matrices in dimensions d >= 3

entries.abstract: Let b(n, l) be the number of parking functions of length n whose maximum displacement is exactly l, where the displacement of a car is the distance between the spot it takes and its preferred spot. The formalization proves in Lean 4 with Mathlib that for every n >= 1 the sequence b(n, 0), b(n, 1), ..., b(n, n-1) is unimodal, which is Conjecture 6.5 of Celano, Elder, Hadaway, Harris, Martin, Priestley and Udell (arXiv:2507.07243). The numbers b(n, l) are defined directly from the parking process. The proof starts from a recursion for the number of parking functions whose maximum displacement is at most a given bound, proved in the library from the parking process, and follows the sign of the difference b(n, k) - b(n, k-1) along columns k as n grows. Rows with n <= 16 and several finite ranges are settled by tables that Lean's kernel evaluates in exact integer arithmetic; analytic estimates, including Robbins' bounds for the factorial, settle the remaining ranges. The proof depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. It was found, written and formalized by AI sessions of an autonomous research system; no person has refereed it.
entries.title: Unimodality of parking functions by maximum displacement

entries.abstract:
We study a particular infinite Ammann–Beenker network, an octagonal mathematical graph with a confining potential. At a special energy it supports two localized wave patterns, A and B. Their normalized sum is called the dark state, and their normalized difference the bright state. Earlier registered results prove that the two patterns account for all independent states at the crossing energy, and that changing a single edge splits this energy while allowing a small part of the bright-derived wave to spread into the rest of the network.

The new theorem asks whether we can prepare any desired mixture of the dark and bright waves without any such spreading. The answer is yes, under two independently adjustable signed real controls. The first changes a common parameter on the eight vertices of the first ring, shifting the energy of A relative to B. The second changes eight genuine edges connecting corresponding sites on the two rings, all by the same amount. These edges are distinct and share no endpoints. Their combined effect leaves the dark state unchanged and shifts the bright energy by twice the edge-strength change. Both controls preserve the original two-state space exactly on the full infinite graph.

The controls change the state in different ways: one mixes the dark and bright amplitudes, while the other changes their relative phase. By applying three consecutive pulses of unit duration (edge control, first-ring control, edge control), we can start with the dark wave and reach any chosen normalized pair of complex dark and bright amplitudes, including the pure bright wave. The final state differs from the desired state only by a common phase of modulus one, which does not change the relative amplitudes or the physical ray. The accumulated phase is given explicitly. The pulse strengths can be chosen from the magnitudes and phases of the desired amplitudes.

The result concerns the actual infinite operator, not a numerical simulation or a two-state approximation. Lean constructs a continuous time-dependent state as two real square-summable graph vectors representing its real and imaginary parts. These vectors lie in the natural domain of the unbounded Hamiltonian at every time and satisfy the coupled full-graph Schrödinger equations during each open pulse interval. The total squared complex norm stays exactly one. The part of each vector outside the original localized two-state space is exactly zero throughout the protocol, including both switching times and the final state. No small-control assumption or pre-existing time-evolution map is required. The Hamiltonian may change discontinuously at the switches, so differentiability at the switching instants is not asserted.

This is an existence theorem for preparation from the dark state in this specified compact plane with independently tunable signed controls. It does not construct a general complex unitary propagator for arbitrary initial data on the infinite graph, prove phase-sensitive equality without a common phase, claim an optimal number of controlled edges, or establish experimental feasibility or originality. The earlier single-edge spectral-splitting theorem is a separate result.

The research direction was conceived and directed by Alessandro Odasso, who is not a mathematician. According to the maintainer, AI generated the mathematical proofs and Lean formalizations under his direction. The originality and scientific significance of these results have not yet been independently assessed.
entries.title: Exact Leakage-Free Quantum State Preparation on an Infinite Ammann–Beenker Graph

entries.abstract: For primes p = 5 (mod 16), p = a^2 + b^2 with b even, the companion note proves h(-8p) = h(-4p) + 8 [b = +-6 (mod 16)] (mod 16), which settles Conjecture 5.3 of Paper V of the K Project series. The proof writes 4(h(-8p) - h(-4p)) as a combination of representation numbers of x^2 + 2y^2 + 4z^2 and x^2 + 2y^2 + 2z^2. It shows that a weight-2 form Phi built from sieved theta series vanishes modulo 256, by Sturm's theorem and a finite check below the bound 512, and reads off the coefficient at p. This development formalizes the proof with the modular input (Serre-Stark modularity and Sturm's theorem) and Gauss's three-square class number formula as explicit hypotheses. It proves the finite check by kernel computation, the iteration of Sturm's theorem, the inversion of theta(1), the bijections relating the ternary forms to sums of three squares, the uniqueness argument for p = a^2 + b^2, the congruence, Conjecture 5.3 given Paper V Theorem 5.2(iv), and the corollaries on the octant sum and with Desnoux's congruence.
entries.title: ConjCoord: a class number congruence modulo 16 for p = 5 (mod 16) and Conjecture coord of Paper V

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the paper 'An 83/84 approximation for three-occurrence Horn formulas above the Unique Games thresholds'. The compared results are: the three-occurrence formula T_H built from a cubic graph, its explicit clause semantics (at most one negative literal per clause, with a proved complement-variable translation to standard Horn clauses that preserves satisfaction), the exact identity OPT(T_H) = 4n + m + alpha, the repair lemma, the number of clauses and the three occurrences of every variable, and the 83/84 approximation ratio transferred from a cubic independent-set guarantee, together with the degree-d ratio arithmetic. The supporting modules also formalize the MAX-CUT reduction, the conflict graph and the lift of a Goemans-Williamson cut to the 83/84 ratio. Goemans-Williamson, Berman-Fujito and the Unique Games thresholds are cited hypotheses, not reproved.
entries.title: PalomaMax2SAT: an 83/84 approximation for three-occurrence Horn formulas above the Unique Games thresholds

entries.abstract: Conjecture 1.2 of C. David, A. Dunn, A. Hamieh and H. Lin (arXiv:2306.11875) asserts that the sums S_beta(X; l) of normalized quartic Gauss sums g(c) over primary primes c of Z[i] with N(c) <= X and c = beta (mod 4), twisted by (conj(c)/|c|)^l and weighted by the von Mangoldt function, are b_beta X^(3/4) + O(X^(1/2+eps)) with b_beta nonzero when l = 0 and O(X^(1/2+eps)) when l is nonzero. The development proves that if g(c)^2 = -kappa c/|c| for a fixed unit kappa on the support of the weight (the identity (1.2) of the same paper), then g(c) conj(c)/|c| = -kappa conj(g(c)), so S_beta(X; 1) = -kappa conj(S_beta(X; 0)), and the cases l = 0 and l = 1 of the conjecture force b_beta = 0, which the conjecture excludes; the same holds when the identity fails on an exceptional set of weight O(X^(1/2+eps)). More generally S_beta(X; 1 - l) = -kappa conj(S_beta(X; l)) for every l. The corrected conjecture, with main term -kappa conj(b_beta) X^(3/4) at l = 1, is shown equivalent under the identity to its cases l <= 0, and that main term is shown to be the only one compatible with the case l = 0. It also proves the pairing identities A(nu^3, -m) = -kappa conj A(nu, m) for the twisted moments and the fact behind the special role of order four: if |g| = 1 and g^k = xi then conj(g) = g^(k-1) conj(xi). The Gauss sum and the von Mangoldt function are abstract functions on the Gaussian integers, so no quartic residue symbol is defined.
entries.title: QuarticPairing: the pairing of the twists in Conjecture 1.2 of David, Dunn, Hamieh and Lin

entries.abstract: For n >= 1 let S_n be the mean of the least residues of the squares modulo n and f(n) = sum_{j <= n/4} floor(sqrt(jn)) - (n^2 - 1)/12. Chamberland and Dilcher (arXiv:2510.04387) evaluated f(p) through class numbers and stated five conjectures for composite n. The development proves, for every n >= 1, the reduction of f(n) to S_n and s(n) = #{k < n : n | k^2} in the four classes of n modulo 4 (lattice points under the parabola and the pairing k -> n - k), and the divisor form of the formula for S_n: (n - s(n))/2 - S_n = sum_{d | n} G(d), where G(d) is a sawtooth sum of phi_d = sum_{e | d} mu(d/e) cnt(e, .) and cnt(e, b) counts the square roots of b modulo e. It proves that G vanishes on d = 1, 2 (mod 4), that G(c) = -(1/c) sum_{a<c} a (-c/a) when -c is a fundamental discriminant, and the conductor recursion G(l^2 c) = (l - (-c/l)) G(c) for every prime l and every c > 0 with c = 0, 3 (mod 4); with Dirichlet's class number formula and the conductor formula (quoted) these give G(c) = h*(-c). It derives Conjectures 7.1 (with the sign of one term corrected), 7.2, 7.3 and 7.4 of Chamberland and Dilcher, their formulas (7.3) and (7.4) for n = pq, Bunyakovsky's identity f(p) = 0 for p = 1 (mod 4) and their Proposition 1.2, with the class numbers in Bernoulli form, and Conjecture 7.5 (the limits of f(n)/n) unconditionally, from the bound defect(n)^2 <= n sqrt(n) (1 + log n)^3, proved with the discrete Fourier transform on Z/n, explicit Fourier coefficients of the sawtooth and Weyl differencing for the quadratic Gauss sums (no class numbers). A second proof of Conjecture 7.5 from the class number bound |G(c)| <= C sqrt(c) (1 + log c), stated as a hypothesis, follows the first proof in the note.
entries.title: MeanResidue: mean quadratic residues, floor sums of square roots and the conjectures of Chamberland and Dilcher

entries.abstract: Sequel to QuadraticFloor. For an odd prime p, the alternating floor sums S_{A,B,C}(p) = sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p) with admissible (B, C) are averages of first Bernoulli numbers of the odd characters vartheta_{p,psi} = eta_p chi_{-4}^delta psi modulo 8Ap. The development proves that, weighted by psi_0(b)^2 and summed over the units b modulo A, these sums give minus the sum of B_{1,vartheta_{p,psi}} over the fibre psi^2 = psi_0^2, which is real when psi_0^4 = 1; that for a prime l = 1 (mod 4), a quartic character xi modulo l and an odd prime p != l the real part of B_{1,Theta_{l,p}}, Theta_{l,p} = vartheta_{p,xi}, and the Bernoulli number of eta_p (./l) are signed combinations of floor sums (the case l = 13 included); the Euler-factor relation B_{1,f 1_{l does not divide}}^{(ml)} = (1 - f(l)) B_{1,f}^{(m)} and the class-number shapes of the coefficients three and five; the quarter-range formula B_{1,vartheta_{p,psi}}^{(8Ap)} = -sum_{0<x<=2Ap} vartheta_{p,psi}(x); and an elementary proof that both coordinates of B_{1,Theta_{l,p}}^{(8lp)} are even integers, for every odd prime p. Every Bernoulli number is taken at a stated modulus; 8lp is the conductor of Theta_{l,p} only for p != l.
entries.title: QuadraticFloorII: fibre sums and quartic traces at conductor 8lp

entries.abstract: Miranda, Movasati, Rufino and Villaflor (arXiv:2609.27301) reduce the Hodge conjecture for Fermat varieties to bounding by six the lengths of certain exceptional classes, and prove it in every degree below 65 except 44, 51 and 52. The length of a class of degree d is the least number of nonzero residues modulo d, with multiplicity, of an element of the free abelian group R_d that differs from it by an element of D_d + S_d, the subgroup generated by the linear and by Aoki's standard tuples. Their tables give the upper bound 7 in degrees 44 and 52. This project proves that the length is exactly 7 for the two given seven-element representatives, so the criterion "length at most six" cannot be met in degrees 44 and 52 without lifting the class to a larger degree. The proof uses additive invariants of R_d that vanish on every generator: one for each unit t, the sum of 2 (t a mod d) - d (Shioda's condition), and the parity of the number of residues of order 11 (degree 44) or 13 (degree 52), which is odd on the representative. An exhaustive check, whose soundness is proved and which the kernel evaluates, shows that no list of at most six residues has those values. The same is proved modulo a larger subgroup, with more standard tuples. Nothing here proves or disproves the Hodge conjecture for any variety.
entries.title: Two exceptional Hodge classes of Fermat varieties have length exactly seven (degrees 44 and 52)

entries.abstract: For an odd prime p and integers A, B, C, the alternating floor sum S_{A,B,C}(p) is the sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p). The development proves the root-count reduction of S_{A,B,C}(p) to a sum of Legendre symbols over an arithmetic progression when A + B is even and p does not divide A, and, for a positive odd A, an odd prime p not dividing A and an admissible pair (B odd, prime to A, 1 <= B^2 - 4AC < 4A), the square-class decomposition: S_{A,B,C}(p) equals (-1)^C minus the average over the Dirichlet characters psi modulo A of conj(psi(B))^2 times the first Bernoulli number, at modulus 8Ap, of the odd character eta_p chi_{-4}^{delta} psi, where eta_p is the Kronecker character of discriminant -8p. Consequently the sum depends only on the square class of B modulo A. At A = 1 and A = 3 this gives the floor sums in terms of Bernoulli numbers of quadratic characters (which are class numbers by Dirichlet's formula, not formalized). At A = 5 the difference S_{5,3,0}(p) - S_{5,1,0}(p) is the real part of the first Bernoulli number of the quartic character Theta_p = eta_p chi_{-4} xi of conductor 40p, with xi(2) = i; this real part is an even integer whose residue modulo 4 is given by an explicit indicator z_1 - z_3. Finally the sums with A = 1 and fixed shifts a, b are classified: for odd a in terms of S_{1,1,0}(p) and an oriented sum of Legendre symbols, for even a by an explicit finite formula that is bounded and eventually constant in p.
entries.title: QuadraticFloor: quadratic floor sums and the trace of a quartic Bernoulli number

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of the formula of Kisielewicz (1988) that writes the Dedekind number M(n), the number of monotone Boolean functions of n variables, as a finite sum of products of binary digits. The formula is proved in two forms: as Formal Conjectures states it, with natural-number arithmetic, and as it is usually printed, with integer arithmetic, digits given by the floor function, and the sum over k from 1 to 2^(2^n). The proof reads k as a family of subsets of an n-element set: the subset coded by the binary digits of i belongs to the family when the i-th digit of k is 1. The innermost product is 1 when the subset coded by i is contained in the subset coded by j, and 0 otherwise. Containment forces i <= j, so only pairs i < j matter: the term of k is 1 when the family is an antichain and 0 otherwise, and the sum counts antichains, which are equinumerous with monotone Boolean functions. The formula is an identity and not a practical algorithm: the sum has 2^(2^n) terms, and no new Dedekind number is computed. The mathematics is classical and no mathematical priority is claimed.
entries.title: Kisielewicz's formula for the Dedekind numbers

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of the Kochen-Specker theorem: for every d at least 3 and for real or complex scalars (any RCLike field), no map from the vectors of the d-dimensional Hilbert space to {true, false} is true on exactly one vector of every orthonormal basis. The map is defined on all vectors, and nothing is assumed about its values off unit vectors or under phases.
