Dimension three uses Peres's 33 rays, coordinates in {0, 1, -1, sqrt 2, -sqrt 2}, kept exactly as integer pairs; their 72 orthogonal pairs and 16 orthogonal triads admit no colouring, which a case-split certificate generated by a script and checked by the Lean kernel shows. A valuation in dimension d + 1 restricts to the orthogonal complement of a unit vector on which it is false, so the theorem passes to every larger dimension, in any inner product space. The case d at least 4 is also proved without computer search, from Cabello, Estebaranz and Garcia-Alcaine's 18 vectors by their parity count. A valuation on R^2 is also constructed, so the hypothesis d at least 3 is needed. Earlier formal proofs cover R^3 (Lean, HOL Light) and C^4 (Lean); this entry gives the statement for every dimension at least 3, over R and C at once. The theorem is on Mathlib's list of 1000+ theorems (docs/1000.yaml, Wikidata Q528955), with no formalization recorded there.
entries.title: The Kochen-Specker theorem in every dimension

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization proving that no odd perfect number N = pi^alpha * q_1^(r-1) * ... * q_t^(r-1) has every non-special prime raised to the same exponent r - 1 for any odd prime 3 <= r <= 73 (all 20 odd primes, 1 <= beta <= 36 where r = 2*beta + 1), together with Kanold's theorem (notSpecial_of_prime) that r cannot be the special prime for any odd prime r >= 3. Independently proves the 9 classical prime cases in this range and settles all 11 remaining prime cases through r = 73 (including beta = 9, 15, 20, 21, 23 left open by Cohen and Williams 1985, plus r = 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, 73). Companion write-up, additional larger certificates through r = 167 (not packaged in this single repository due to certificate size), and dated literature search logs are published at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/odd-perfect-equal-exponents.
entries.title: Odd Perfect Numbers: Equal Non-Special Exponents for Every Odd Prime 3 <= r <= 73

entries.abstract: Kisielewicz's weak double extension set theory DEST has two membership relations and interprets ZF; its consistency was an open problem. This Lean 4 formalization (core only) proves that DEST is inconsistent, already without its regularity axiom. Comprehension alone, in intuitionistic logic, refutes every formula that is asymmetric between the two relations (DEST.diagonal); with mixed extensionality and classical logic, given as an explicit hypothesis, the ordinals are asymmetric, so DEST without regularity has no model (DEST.inconsistent), and neither has full DEST (DEST.DEST_inconsistent).
entries.title: Weak double extension set theory is inconsistent

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the main results, Theorems 2.1–2.4, of Erdős, Yau and Yin, "Rigidity of eigenvalues of generalized Wigner matrices" (Adv. Math. 229 (2012), arXiv:1007.4652), for real symmetric and complex hermitian generalized Wigner matrices with independent entries, variances summing to one in each row, a spectral gap of the variance matrix and uniform subexponential decay. Theorem 2.1: the strong local semicircle law |m - m_sc| <= (log N)^{4L} / (N eta) down to the optimal scale, its entrywise form, and the bound on the extreme eigenvalues. Theorem 2.2: rigidity of the eigenvalues, |lambda_j - gamma_j| <= (log N)^L min(j, N-j+1)^{-1/3} N^{-2/3} for all j, and the corresponding bound on the counting function, each with probability at least 1 - C exp(-c (log N)^{phi L}). Theorem 2.3: strong local ergodicity of Dyson Brownian motion in the bulk, for times t >= N^{-1+delta+epsilon'}. Theorem 2.4: universality of the largest and of the smallest eigenvalue for two ensembles whose entries have matching first and second moments. No result of another work is assumed; the results the paper cites, in particular the local relaxation flow, are proved in the library from Mathlib.
entries.title: Rigidity of eigenvalues of generalized Wigner matrices

entries.abstract:
The node f(w) = w1 w2 on the closed unit square [0,1]^2 has one distinguished function, P(s) = -log s. This entry proves in Lean 4 and Mathlib that P is the density of states of the node, and that the zeta function, partition function and free energy of the toy singular learning model K(w) = (w1 w2)^2 with uniform prior on [0,1]^2 are explicit transforms of it; it also states the monodromy of the logarithm in Mathlib's covering-space sense, and treats the general monomial (normal-crossing) zeta function and free energy. Eleven statements are compared.
(1) Density of states: the pushforward of Lebesgue measure on [0,1]^2 under w -> w1 w2 equals the measure on (0,1] with density -log s. (The function -log s is also the integral over the fibre {w1 w2 = s} of the Gelfand–Leray form dw1/w1; this interpretation is not separately stated.) (2) For real z, the learning zeta function zeta(z) = integral over [0,1]^2 of ((w1 w2)^2)^z is finite (the integrand is integrable) if and only if z > -1/2, and (3) for z > -1/2 it equals 1/(2z+1)^2. The closed form has a double pole at -1/2, which in Watanabe's singular learning theory corresponds to learning coefficient 1/2 and multiplicity 2; meromorphic continuation is not stated. (4)-(6) Monomial (normal-crossing) zeta function. For natural numbers k_1, ..., k_d, real h_1, ..., h_d, K(w) = prod_j w_j^(2 k_j) and the (unnormalized) prior density phi(w) = prod_j w_j^(h_j) on [0,1]^d: (4) K^z phi is integrable on the cube if and only if 2 k_j z + h_j + 1 > 0 for every j (real z); (5) then zeta(z) = integral of K^z phi = prod_j 1/(2 k_j z + h_j + 1); and (6) if all k_j > 0, lambda = min_j (h_j + 1)/(2 k_j) and m >= 1 is the number of indices attaining it, then (z + lambda)^m zeta(z) tends to a nonzero limit as z -> -lambda from above, i.e. zeta has a pole of order exactly m at -lambda (real variable, one-sided). This is the normal-crossing form to which singular learning theory reduces a model after resolution of singularities, where (lambda, m) are the learning coefficient and its multiplicity; the resolution step is not formalized. (2)-(3) are the case d = 2, k = (1,1), h = 0, stated on R x R and proved separately through (1). (10)-(11) Monomial free energy: for the same models with all k_j > 0 and h_j > -1, the partition function Z(n) = integral over [0,1]^d of exp(-n K) phi satisfies Z(n) = Theta(n^(-lambda) (log n)^(m-1)) as real n -> infinity (upper and lower bounds by constant multiples), so F(n) = -log Z(n) = lambda log n - (m - 1) log log n + O(1). This is Watanabe's free-energy asymptotic for models in normal-crossing form; the node's (7)-(8) are its d = 2 instance, sharpened there to exact constants. The proof is an induction on the dimension, integrating out one coordinate at a time with one-variable Laplace-type estimates. (7) Sharp partition function: Z(n) = integral over [0,1]^2 of exp(-n (w1 w2)^2) satisfies Z(n) = (sqrt(pi)/(4 sqrt(n))) (log n + gamma + 2 log 2) + O(exp(-n)) as real n -> infinity, where gamma is the Euler–Mascheroni constant. (8) Free energy: F(n) = -log Z(n) satisfies F(n) - (1/2 log n - log log n) -> log(4/sqrt(pi)), the form lambda log n - (m - 1) log log n + O(1) of Watanabe's asymptotics with lambda = 1/2, m = 2, here with the exact constant. (9) Monodromy of the logarithm: for Mathlib's covering map exp from the complex plane to the punctured plane and the loop theta -> exp(2 pi i theta) based at 1, IsCoveringMap.monodromy sends the fibre point 0 to 2 pi i. Lifts through exp are continuations of log, so P = -log continues to P - 2 pi i around s = 0: the unipotent monodromy of the node's period.
In the Lean development, (2), (3), (7) and (8) are derived from the same transfer lemma, a consequence of (1): an integral over the square of a function of w1 w2 equals the integral over (0,1] of that function against -log s. The zeta function is then the Mellin transform of -log s and the partition function its Gaussian Laplace transform. The exact constant in (7) comes from Mathlib's value of the derivative of the Gamma function at 1/2. Scope: real variables throughout; (1)-(3) and (7)-(8) concern one explicit model with uniform prior on the closed unit square, and (4)-(6), (10)-(11) monomial models on the closed unit cube; resolution of singularities, the reduction of general models to normal-crossing form (hence the free-energy asymptotic for general models), b-functions and Picard–Lefschetz theory are not formalized, and (9) is the monodromy of the logarithm itself, not of a family of cycles. All results are classical or elementary consequences of classical results; we searched the Palomar registry and Mathlib (November 2026) and found no prior formalization of them, but did not search other sources, so priority among Lean formalizations is unknown.
entries.title: One node, one density: the density of states of w1 w2 on the unit square; the zeta function, sharp partition function and free energy of the singular learning model K = (w1 w2)^2; and the zeta function, learning coefficient, multiplicity and free energy of monomial (normal-crossing) models

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the main result of Yau and Yin, "The Second Order Upper Bound for the Ground Energy of a Bose Gas" (J. Stat. Phys. 136 (2009), arXiv:0903.5347). For N bosons in the box [0, L]^3 with periodic boundary condition, interacting through a pair potential V that is a nonnegative even Schwartz function, not identically zero and small enough that the Born series converges, the ground state energy per particle e_0 satisfies limsup_{rho -> 0+} limsup_{L -> infinity, N/L^3 -> rho} (e_0 - g_0 rho) / (g_0^{5/2} rho^{3/2}) <= 16/(15 pi^2), where g_0 = int V(1 - w) = 4 pi a, 1 - w is the zero-energy scattering solution and a is the scattering length. This is the upper bound in the Lee–Huang–Yang formula e_0 = 4 pi a rho (1 + (128/(15 sqrt(pi))) (rho a^3)^{1/2} + ...). The formalization also proves that the zero-energy scattering solution exists and is unique under these hypotheses, that the Gaussian potential satisfies them, and that the statement is not vacuous (g_0 > 0, the energies are nonnegative, the filter of the thermodynamic limit is proper). Everything the paper takes as known (scattering theory, Riemann sums on the dual lattice, the variational principle, the passage between periodic and Dirichlet boundary conditions) is proved in the library from Mathlib.

entries.abstract: Let u_1 < u_2 < ... be the positive integers with at most two prime factors, counted with multiplicity. Erdős Problem 1139 asks whether limsup (u_{k+1} - u_k) / log k = infinity. This formalization proves that it is, in the formulation of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Erdos1139.erdos_1139). The proof is an Erdős-Rankin style construction: the Chinese remainder theorem gives N such that every number in a long interval N + 1, ..., N + y is given a divisor below it with exactly two prime factors (two assigned primes, or the square of one), and so has at least three prime factors, with log N small compared to y. The residues of the small primes are chosen by averaging over all assignments, with Euler-product weights and smooth-number bounds; larger primes are grouped into bands and handled by a second-moment argument; the few remaining numbers are patched with squares of reserve primes. No results on linear equations in primes are used.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 1139: unbounded gaps between integers with at most two prime factors

entries.abstract: For a prime p = 1 (mod 8) and a quartic character chi modulo p (even, with w = chi(2) = +-1), the development proves that the coordinates of B_(2,chi) = c0 + i c1 are integers with c0 = 4(E_1 + E_-1), c1 = 4(E_i + E_-i) and c0 + c1 = p - 1 modulo 8, and that 8 divides both exactly when w = 1, i.e. when 2 is a fourth power. entries.abstract: For an integer r >= 2 and a finite set N of primes, the random Euler product model for Dirichlet characters of order r replaces chi(q) by independent uniform r-th roots of unity. The development proves that the order-r local factor E|1 - z/q|^(-2) equals (1 + q^-r)/((1 - q^-2)(1 - q^-r)), that its ratio to the full-circle factor (1 - q^-2)^(-1), multiplied over the primes outside N, is zeta^(N)(r)^2 / zeta^(N)(2r), that this correction factor is also the sum of (ab)^-r over the coprime pairs of integers prime to N, and that the model mean is zeta^(N)(2) zeta^(N)(r)^2 / zeta^(N)(2r). The factor exceeds 1, decreases strictly in r and tends to 1; for r = 2k and N empty it equals -binom(4k,2k) B_{2k}^2/(2 B_{4k}). For r = 4 and N = {2} it is 35/34, the ratio by which the limit of Louboutin's mean square of L(1, chi) with the factor at 2 removed changes when the average is restricted to quartic characters; with the forced factor 4/5 at 2 the development also proves the constants pi^2/10, 7 pi^2/68, 7 pi^2/36 and 7/136 = (1/20)(35/34) = (7/72)(9/17). It also identifies the pairs the model keeps: for positive m, n the average of z^m conj(z^n) is 1 exactly when m/n is an r-th power in Q, that is when (m, n) = (d a^r, d b^r) with a, b coprime, and 0 otherwise. Modulo a single prime p with r | p - 1 it proves the finite-character counterpart: there are exactly r Dirichlet characters mod p with chi^r = 1, the sum of chi(a) conj(chi(b)) over them is r when a/b is a nonzero r-th power mod p and 0 otherwise, so every pair (d a^r, d b^r) prime to p survives with sum r; by contrast, summed over all characters mod p, chi(m) conj(chi(n)) has sum 0 for distinct m, n < p. Release v1.2 adds the finite part of the Chebyshev bias in families p = a (mod M) of fixed order r: with rho_s(t) the average of exp(2 pi i u t/s) over the units u mod s, the sum over t < s of rho_s(c t) is s when s | c and 0 otherwise; for M > 0 and s | M the squares in Z/s x| (Z/M)^x give the prime-square term of the explicit formula as s times the square-root count beta(M, a, s) = #{y in (Z/M)^x : y^2 = a, y = -1 (mod s)}, a count of residue classes (the same finite-sum identity over the representatives 0 <= x < M holds for all M and s > 0, but is only an arithmetic identity there: vacuous at M = 0, representative-dependent when s does not divide M); beta does not decrease as s decreases along divisibility, at s = r it is 0 unless a is a square in H = ker((Z/M)^x -> (Z/r)^x) and is then the number of square roots of 1 in H; and for the imaginary families (r even, M = 2r, a = 1 + r) beta vanishes for every s unless 8 | r, and for s = r/d with d odd in every case.

entries.abstract:
The Legendre family of elliptic curves y^2 = x(x-1)(x-λ) has the period function F(λ) = 2F1(1/2, 1/2; 1; λ), taken here as Mathlib's ordinaryHypergeometric. Its Picard–Fuchs operator is λ(1-λ) y'' + (1-2λ) y' - y/4. The second Frobenius solution at λ = 0 is L(λ) = F(λ) log λ + G(λ), with G(λ) = sum over n of a_n h_n λ^n, a_n = (C(2n,n)/4^n)^2 the Taylor coefficients of F, and h_n = sum_{k=1}^{n} 2/(k(2k-1)). Let D be the slit unit disc, the open unit disc minus (-1, 0]. This entry proves, in Lean 4 and Mathlib, seven statements.
(1) F is holomorphic on the unit disc and solves the Picard–Fuchs equation there. (2) Period integral: for |λ| < 1, F(λ) = (1/π) ∫_0^1 dx / (sqrt(x(1-x)) (1-λx)^{1/2}), with the principal branch of the complex power. (3) Wronskian: F L' - F' L = 1/(λ(1-λ)) on D. (4) Solution space: a function y is holomorphic on D and solves the Picard–Fuchs equation on D if and only if y = aF + bL on D for some complex constants a, b. (5) F and L are linearly independent on D. (6) Local monodromy at 0: there is a function holomorphic on the unit disc slit along [0, 1) that equals L on the open upper half-disc and L + 2πi F on the open lower half-disc; that is, L continues analytically across (-1, 0) to L + 2πi F, while F is holomorphic on the whole disc. In the basis (F, L), the local monodromy at 0 is therefore [[1, 2πi], [0, 1]]. (7) Connection formula: on the lens where |λ| < 1 and |λ - 1| < 1, F(1-λ) = (4 log 2 · F(λ) - L(λ))/π. This expresses the solution regular at λ = 1 in the Frobenius basis at λ = 0; its constants come from the classical asymptotic K(k) = log(4/k') + o(1) as k → 1, which is proved here from the period integral.
The proofs are a power-series treatment of the equation and of G (whose coefficients satisfy a harmonic-number recursion), Abel's identity for the Wronskian, a uniqueness theorem for holomorphic solutions with vanishing Cauchy data at an ordinary point (derivative recursion, Taylor series and the identity theorem; Mathlib's ODE uniqueness is for real time only), term-by-term integration of the binomial series against Beta integrals, and an explicit estimate of the complete elliptic integral near its logarithmic singularity. All seven results are classical; this is, to our knowledge, their first Lean formalization. Scope: everything is local to λ = 0 (and, for (7), to the lens); the global monodromy group Γ(2) and analytic continuation along paths are not formalized; the elliptic curve, its differential forms and its homology do not appear, so "period" refers to the integral formula (2).
entries.title: The Legendre family: Picard–Fuchs equation, period integral, solution space, local monodromy and connection formula for 2F1(1/2,1/2;1;λ)

entries.abstract: For an odd prime p, an odd character chi modulo p and m >= 0, the multiplier family C(a) = sum over 0 < n < p/2 of chi(n) (-1)^(n + <a n^(2m)>) has Fourier transform over the characters 2 sum_a conj(psi)(a) C(a) = G(conj psi) G(chi psi^(2m)), with the multiplier constant G(psi) = sum_m psi(m) (-1)^m, which is 2 (1 - 2 psi(2)) B_(1,psi) for odd psi and 0 for even psi (the Bernoulli expression is false for even psi). entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization (514 audited declarations, zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only) resolving all four questions and observations (Q1, Q2, O1, O2) from Badkobeh and Ochem (Theoret. Comput. Sci. 588, 2015) for the 5-letter morphic fixed point b5 = f5^omega(0) (0 -> 01, 1 -> 23, 2 -> 4, 3 -> 21, 4 -> 0). The library identifies b5 as the exact 5-interval coding of a golden-ratio 3-interval exchange on (-phi^2/2, phi^3/2) via the -1/phi left eigenvector, proving unconditionally that (Q1) b5 has exact factor complexity 4n + 1 for every n >= 0, (O1) g_fib(b5) has the exact same factors as the Fibonacci word with complexity n + 1, (O2) g_rf(b5) has the exact same factors as the Rote-Fibonacci word with complexity 2n for n >= 1, and (Q2) the critical exponent of b5 is exactly (5 + sqrt(5))/4 and is strictly unattained. entries.abstract: Formalization of dimension-independent exponential entropy-quotient bounds for laws on finite vector spaces over F₂. For every ε > 0 a subspace of dimension at most 2^(320(1+ε)/ε) H(X) makes the quotient entropy at most (1+ε) times its independent-doubling entropy increment, which does not exceed the original increment. The development also proves logarithmic rigidity for sparse laws and finite weighted families, necessity of exponential dependence on 1/ε, two-input almost-additivity, and concentration of moderate-doubling sets on subspace cosets. Entropies are in bits. The entropic Marton input is obtained from the pinned PFR formalization through a proved translation to probability mass functions. The selected results are Theorems 1.1, 1.2 and 8.2, Proposition 9.3, and Corollaries 9.2 and 9.4 of arXiv:2610.38525v1; no optimality of the constant 320 is claimed.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the main results of Dubova, Yang, Yau and Yin, "Delocalization of two-dimensional random band matrices" (arXiv:2503.07606). The model is the complex Gaussian block band matrix on the torus Z_L^2 with L^2 blocks of size W x W, N = W^2 L^2, and band width W >= N^c for some c > 0. This entry contains Theorem 2.2 (delocalization of the bulk eigenvectors), Theorem 2.3 (the local semicircle law, (4)-(5)), Theorem 2.4 (generalized quantum unique ergodicity, (8)-(9)) and Theorem 2.5 (quantum diffusion, (10)-(13)); they have no hypotheses other than their parameters, and no result of another work is assumed for them. The library also proves Theorem 2.6 (bulk universality) from one external input, stated as an explicit hypothesis; that theorem is not part of this entry.

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the two main theorems of Chen, McDonald, and Shan. Theorem 1.3 proves the overfull criterion for sufficiently large robust expanders with linear maximum degree, weak Vizing adjacency, and few vertices of large degree deficit. Theorem 1.4 gives the criterion for sufficiently large simple graphs whose maximum degree is at least (1 + epsilon) times half the order, for every fixed positive epsilon. The proof includes the reduction to critical graphs, the two stopping routes, and the coloring of the canonical completion.

entries.abstract: For a prime p = 5 (mod 8) let chi be the quartic Dirichlet character with chi(2) = i, with values in the Gaussian integers, and let C(p) = f + i e be the sum of chi(n) (-1)^floor(n^2/p) over 0 < n < p/2. The development proves that f = (p-1)/4 (mod 4) and e = kappa (mod 4) for every such p, where kappa is the sum of the Legendre symbols (n/p) over 0 < n < p/4. The mechanism is a matching lemma: for sign functions sigma, tau and a bijection pi, the correlation sum sigma(x) tau(pi x) is congruent modulo 4 to the sum of the two marginals minus the number of terms, so it does not depend on pi. Along the way it proves the parity dictionary (-1)^floor(n^2/p) = s(n) s(n^2) with s(x) = (-1)^<x>, the coset form f = sum over the fourth powers H of s(u) s(u^2) and e = the same sum over 2H, the lag identity sum over 2H of s(u) s(2u) = kappa exactly, the exact coset parities sum_H s = k + 2t and sum_{2H} s = t - 2k where B_{1,chi} = k + i t, and the Coordinate Congruence kappa = (p-1)/4 + k + t (mod 4). It also proves the odd-subgroup congruence: for an odd modulus N >= 3, a subgroup H of (Z/N)^x of odd order h, a coset X = xH and an even exponent e >= 2, the band-parity sum of X and -X over (0, N/2) equals sum over X of s(u) s(u^e) and is congruent to h - 2 alpha(X) - 2 alpha(X^e) modulo 4, where alpha counts elements with odd least residue.

entries.abstract: For k >= 2 and a subgroup H of odd order n of the unit group (Z/kZ)^x, the sum S(H,k) of the Dedekind sums s(h,k) over h in H satisfies: 12k S(H,k) is an integer congruent to n(k-1)(k-2) modulo 16, and the modulus 16 cannot be replaced by 32 (an explicit pair of order-3 subgroups of (Z/63Z)^x). The development also proves a congruence modulo 8 for every subgroup, a congruence for 2k S(H,k) when 3 does not divide k, and, for primes p > 3 and n > 1, that 2S(H,p) is an integer congruent to n(p-1)/2 modulo 8, which refines Louboutin's parity theorem and gives 12S(H,p) - p congruent to 3n(p-1) - p modulo 48. The proof formalizes Meyer's formula 12k s(h,k) = (k-1)(k-2) - 4I(h,k), where I(h,k) counts the inversions of x -> hx mod k, and the facts that these inversion counts are even on squares and equal for inverse elements.

entries.abstract: Conjecture 213 of DeLaViña's Written on the Wall II (Graffiti.pc) says that a simple connected graph G on n > 1 vertices has a Hamiltonian path if 2 + lm(Ḡ) ≤ γ₂(Ḡ), where Ḡ is the complement of G, lm(Ḡ) the lower median of the degree sequence of Ḡ and γ₂(Ḡ) the 2-domination number of Ḡ. The package proves the conjecture as stated, with no hypothesis beyond the source's. The main theorem reads the lower median as the middle term d_{⌈n/2⌉} of the degree sequence (d_{n/2} for even n, the median d_{(n+1)/2} for odd n). For odd n the catalogue's definition 68 names the term d_{(n+1)/2+1}, which is not the middle term; that literal reading is proved as a variant theorem, which follows from the main one because the literal term is never smaller.
entries.title: WOWII Conjecture 213 holds (a Hamiltonian path)

entries.abstract: Unconditional pure core Lean 4 formalization (zero external dependencies, zero Mathlib imports, zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only) determining the exact last exception c*(k) for the 2-colour Rado number R(c, k) of x + y + c = kz for every integer k >= 3, where c*(k) = k(k^2 + k - 4)/2 for odd k and k(k^2 - 2)/2 for even k. Both halves are formalized unconditionally: (1) an original reflection proof (x |-> N+1-x) of the upper half R(c, k) = LB(c, k) for every valid c > c*(k) (valid means k odd or c even), and (2) Martinelli and Schaal's (2007) Lemma 3 lower half showing non-forcing at LB(c*(k), k), i.e., there exists a 2-colouring of [1, LB(c*(k), k)] with no monochromatic solution of x + y + c*(k) = k z (so ¬ Forced (c*(k)) k (LB (c*(k)) k) and c*(k) is an exception to R(c, k) = LB(c, k); finite existence of R(c*(k), k) itself is not formalized). In nu_iff, the property "R(c, k) = LB(c, k) for all valid c >= v" holds iff c*(k) < v, so the least integer cutoff is c*(k) + 1 while the least valid cutoff nu(k) (requiring Valid nu(k) k, i.e., even when k is even) is c*(k) + 1 for odd k and c*(k) + 2 for even k, giving least valid cutoffs 13, 30, 66, 104, 183, 250, 388, 492 for k = 3..10 and settling the Kim-Song-Hwang (2023) conjecture nu(5) = 66.
