entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the planar separator theorem of Lipton and Tarjan and of nested dissection. A plane graph is a Mathlib simple graph on a finite vertex type with a rotation system (a permutation of the darts cycling the darts at each vertex) such that the graph is connected and Euler's formula |V| + |F| = |E| + 2 holds for the set F of faces (so it has at least one edge: faces are cycles of darts, and the one-vertex graph has none). Eight theorems are compared: (1) the separator theorem with constant 6: for nonnegative vertex weights of total at most 1, a set of at most 6 sqrt(n) vertices splits the n vertices into two parts with no edge between them, each of weight at most 2/3; (2) the same for every set U of vertices, with at most 6 sqrt(|U|) vertices of U; (3) every plane graph has a separator tree covering all vertices in which every subtree with k vertices has a separator (or leaf set) and a boundary of at most 50000 sqrt(k) vertices each and parts of at most 2k/3 vertices; (4) the same for the square of a plane graph of maximum degree at most D, with 40 (1062 (D + 1)^2 + 1) in place of 50000; (5) for any separator tree with constants alpha and beta, the filled graph of elimination in its nested dissection order has at most alpha (alpha + beta) n (1 + log_{3/2} n) edges; (6), (7) for every plane graph, and for the square of every plane graph of maximum degree at most D, there are a separator tree covering all vertices and the permutation listing its nested dissection order such that the filled graph of that order has at most 2 T^2 n (1 + log_{3/2} n) edges (T as in (3) and (4)), and, for every matrix over a field whose off-diagonal nonzero entries are edges of the graph, permuted into that order, elimination restricted to the filled graph computes exactly the matrix after the n in-place elimination steps M_ij - M_ik M_kk^(-1) M_kj, with at most 48 T^3 n^(3/2) ring operations counted in a writer monad that charges every addition, subtraction, negation, multiplication and inversion of the explicit algorithm; the inverse is Lean's totalized field inverse (0^(-1) = 0), so these steps are Gaussian elimination without pivoting when the pivots are nonzero and leave the matrix unchanged at a zero pivot; (8) one fixed word program (no real instruction) for an explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, natural registers and memory cells bounded by W along the run) prints, for a plane graph with n vertices, m darts and natural vertex weights, a separator of at most 6 sqrt(n) + 3 vertices whose two parts each weigh at most 2/3 of the total, within 320m + 191n + 403 steps for word bounds at least 16m + 12n + 3 (total weight) + 22. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: The planar separator theorem and nested dissection, with a linear-time separator program on a word RAM, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization (zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only) establishing two explicit 37-digit Zhang K2 strong pseudoprimes n1 = 2481162833436289154832260656117034821 (121 bits) and n2 = 5959902256870799858089729225626992341 (123 bits) to the first 20 prime bases (2 through 71, defined via Mathlib's Nat.nth Nat.Prime), giving the upper bound psi_20 <= n1 < 2^121 (OEIS A014233). All four prime factors are certified inside the Lean kernel via Pratt certificates backed by Mathlib's lucas_primality, and both witnesses are proved to fail the strong test at the 21st prime 73 while passing Fermat at 73. The K2 Fermat and 2-adic order criteria formalize specializations of Gerhard Jaeschke's 1993 results. The companion manuscript also presents the exact strong-liar fraction (1 + 2*4^(-e))/6 and base-2 cap <= 3/16, the exact sieve count A(b) and 10,135,125-class wheel mod 401,120,980,260, the Jacobsthal character sum -(2/b) with exact b mod 8 cell counts, and the K_{a/b} Legendre obstruction. Lean covers 6 of the manuscript's 8 main claims. The other 2 are external sieve computations. AI research agents built and directed by Tyler B. Hughes generated and checked the work. No human mathematician has yet refereed the proof. Companion manuscript and verification archive: https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/spsp-psi20.
entries.title: Two 37-Digit 20-Base Strong Pseudoprimes (psi_20 <= n1 < 2^121), Order Criteria, and Exact Sieve Laws

entries.abstract: Conjecture 399b of DeLaViña's Written on the Wall II (Graffiti.pc) says that every connected graph G on n > 2 vertices satisfies γ₂(G) ≤ WP(Ḡ) + ⌊3/α(G[A₃])⌋, where γ₂ is the 2-domination number, WP(Ḡ) the Welsh–Powell invariant of the complement (the largest k with k + d_k ≤ n, the degrees of G taken in nondecreasing order) and A₃ the set of vertices of degree at least three. The package proves the negation, for connected graphs on more than two vertices whose set A₃ is nonempty, with a connected graph F₃ on 12 vertices (graph6 KCOfFFb?~?[?) that has γ₂ = 7, WP(Ḡ) = 6 and α(G[A₃]) = 4, so that 7 > 6 = 6 + ⌊3/4⌋.
entries.title: WOWII Conjecture 399b is false (a 12-vertex counterexample)

entries.abstract: A Boolean function f of n variables is BLF if f(x) is bit j of K + a_1 x_1 + ... + a_n x_n for some integers K, a_i and some bit position j. The development proves, for every n, that the floors of (K + a.x) / 2^j satisfy every parallelogram inequality on the cube, that every threshold function is BLF, and that BLF is closed under XOR with GF(2)-affine functions; and it proves the exact counts |BLF(n)| = 4, 16, 208 and 10368 for n = 1, 2, 3 and 4 by a verified pruned search checked by the kernel, that BLF(3) is exactly the threshold functions XOR GF(2)-affine functions, and that BLF(4) adds exactly the affine translates of bit 1 of x1 + x2 + x3 + x4, which is not itself threshold XOR affine. It also proves, for every n, that f is BLF iff f = floor(t + r.x) mod 2 for real t and r; the selector lemma (z AND T(x) is bit j of an integer affine form iff T has integer weights with sum of absolute values below 2^j), with a gated threshold showing that no bit position below 4 serves every BLF function of five variables; and, through a square identity, that two and three steps of Rule 110 are not BLF.
entries.title: BLF: Boolean functions that are one bit of a linear form

entries.abstract: Repeated uses of the diagonal parity phase from the roots of X⁴−X−1 on the balanced two-qubit product state give squared concurrences dense in the unit interval after every finite cutoff. No finite iterate has the two-step Hardy-optimal Schmidt spectrum. An explicit population change on the first qubit gives that spectrum in one use of the same gate.
entries.title: The Quartic Gate and the Two-Step Hardy Optimum

entries.abstract: Formalization of Basic Functional Categories, Functional Categories, the pointfree CoEndoYoneda Isomorphism Theorem, and its equivalence with computational purity (monad idempotency) for Kleisli categories. Given a category C and a functional functor FF : Type u ⥤ C, we define the CoYoneda endofunctor CYEF(Z) = CYF(Z) ⋙ FF, the global-like endofunctor G = CYEF(FF(T)), and prove the CoEndoYoneda isomorphism (CYEF(Z) ⟶ (EF ⋙ G)) ≃ (FF(T) ⟶ G(EF(Z))). We prove that evaluating the forward isomorphism on id_G recovers the terminal unit component η.app(FF(T)), verify that Type u with the identity functor is a canonical Functional Category, and prove that for the Kleisli category KleisliCat M of a lawful monad M with canonical identity-on-objects functor KFF, BasicFunctionalCategory (KleisliCat M) (KFF M) holds if and only if M is an idempotent (pure) monad. Finally, we derive the terminal subsingleton theorem (IsPure M → Subsingleton (M T)) and classify seven standard computational effects (Option, List, Read, Write, State, Cont, and ErrorState/IO).
entries.title: The CoEndoYoneda Lemma and its Relationship to Purity for Kleisli Categories with an Idempotent Monad

entries.abstract: In a finite split graph whose host neighborhoods are independent in the residual core graph, a proper assignment missing L required pairs realizes the residual integral-fractional packing gap to within 2L. Deleting q crossing edges from a complete assignment changes the gap by at most 2q. For a split presentation with core size c and at least 2c hosts, the gap is at most twice the sum of endpoint omissions in excess of floor(c/2).
entries.title: Stability of the Clique Partition Gap in Split Graphs

entries.abstract: A crystalline tempered distribution on a positive-dimensional Euclidean space is a finite sum of translated and modulated full-rank lattice Dirac combs with complex coefficients if and only if its support and spectrum each admit a polynomial count of degree equal to the dimension in one closed half-ball along divergent radii. The two unit normals and the two radius sequences may be chosen independently. The geometric result gives a single bound on the number of sites of a locally finite set in the measured half-space in every open unit ball, from its ordered patch-volume bound and its half-ball count. Distinct sites may be arbitrarily close.
entries.title: Independent physical and spectral half-ball counts characterize finite sums of lattice combs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the main results of Yang, Yau and Yin, "Delocalization and quantum diffusion of random band matrices in high dimensions I: Self-energy renormalization" (arXiv:2104.12048), proved together with part "II: T-expansion" (arXiv:2107.05795). The model is the Gaussian random band matrix on the torus Z_L^d with band width W and a variance profile given by a symmetric Schwartz function, for L^{c_1} <= W <= L^{1-c_0}. For every dimension d >= 8: Theorem 1.3 of part I (weak delocalization of the bulk eigenvectors, (1.12) and (1.13)), Theorem 1.4 (the local law (1.19), down to eta = W^2 / L^{2-eps}), and Theorem 1.5 with Corollaries 1.6 and 1.7 (quantum diffusion: the expansion of E T_{xy} and E|G_{xy}|^2 with the renormalized diffusive matrix, the bounds on the self-energies, and the diffusion approximation in Fourier space). No result of another work is assumed; every result that the papers use is proved in the library from Mathlib.
entries.title: Delocalization and quantum diffusion of random band matrices in high dimensions

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the main results of Yau and Yin, "Delocalization of one-dimensional random band matrices" (arXiv:2501.01718). The model is the complex Gaussian block band matrix with L blocks of size W, N = WL, and band width W >= N^{1/2+c}. This entry contains Theorem 2.2 (delocalization of the bulk eigenvectors, (2.10)), Theorem 2.3 (the local semicircle law, (2.3)-(2.4)), Theorem 2.4 (quantum diffusion, (2.6)-(2.9)) and Theorem 2.5 (quantum unique ergodicity, (2.12)-(2.13)); they have no hypotheses other than their parameters, and no result of another work is assumed for them. The library also proves Theorem 2.6 (bulk universality) from one external input, stated as an explicit hypothesis; that theorem is not part of this entry.
entries.title: Delocalization of one-dimensional random band matrices

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the main results of A. Languasco, J. Pintz and A. Zaccagnini, On the sum of two primes and k powers of two, Bull. London Math. Soc. 39, 2007, pages 771 to 780, conditional on three results of the literature that the paper cites. For k >= 1 the entry proves that all but O of X^{3/5} times log X to the power 10 even N <= X are sums of two primes and k powers of two; the paper's main theorem, the asymptotic formula for the weighted number of such representations outside an exceptional set of the same size, on the even N in J of X = [2X/3, X], with the main term coefficient 2 c0 C of k and N, where c0 is the twin prime constant; and Corollary 4.2 of the paper on the major arcs. The three cited inputs are explicit hypotheses, never axioms: the explicit formula of Lemma 4.1 of the paper, which it quotes from J. Pintz, ELAZ 2004, Theorem 10; the zero density theorem of M. Jutila 1977, Theorem 1, display 1.8, as printed; and the zero free region of H. Iwaniec 1974, Theorem 2, page 97, as printed, read for nonreal characters. The real zero bound for real characters, which the paper cites from Pintz 1976 and Goldfeld and Schinzel 1975, is proved here from Siegel's theorem. The coefficient 2 c0 C of k and N is the one that the paper's own display 2 gives; the printed theorem states C of k and N in [1, 2] and omits the factor 2 c0, and the entry does not claim the range [1, 2]. Binary Goldbach, the case k = 0, is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic with a few leaves from other lab provers listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: On the sum of two primes and k powers of two

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of Carmichael's totient conjecture lower-bound and density-transfer theory (zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only): proves 10^10,117 < x unconditionally for every Carmichael counterexample x (10^10,240 < x in Case I and 10^10,117 < x in Case II via 161 kernel-checked Lucas primality ladders, surpassing Masai and Valette's 1982 bound of 10^10,000), the unconditional pure-kernel limiting singleton density bound liminf V1(X)/V(X) < 10^-5,057, totient-value and density transfer via Ford's (1998) Lemmas 7.4-7.5 and Chebyshev's prime lower bound, Ford's Lemma 7.2 prime-square forcing rule, Klee's (1947) minimal-counterexample structure, Pomerance's (1974) sufficient condition, Ford's reduction to k = 6, and the unconditional bound m >= 32,000 for Ford's k = 10 divisible-preimage problem, plus non-vacuity witnesses. Scope note: the larger 10^100,000,160,994 Carmichael bound, 10^-50,000,080,497 density bound, and m >= 10^60 k = 10 bound in the companion manuscript (https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/carmichael-totient) rely on external exact-integer certificates whose soundness and transfer theorems are proved in this library.
entries.title: Carmichael's Totient Conjecture: Kernel-Verified 10^10,117 Lower Bound, 10^-5,057 Density Bound, Structural Theory, and Ford's k = 10 Descent

entries.abstract: For an N-vertex graph G, let z = log N and F = max(1, rank over F₂ of its zero-diagonal adjacency matrix divided by z). There are absolute positive constants b,c such that F ≤ c(log z)^(1/3) implies reg(G) > z^(1+b/F) for all sufficiently large N, uniformly in G and F. The formalization proves the fixed-rank and critical-rank corollaries, a sparse off-diagonal error reduction with retained order N²/(2N+4e), and the corresponding strict uniform bound and its particular consequences for minimum binary rank over diagonal completions. The proof constructs physical trace cells, proves their mixing and candidate estimates, replaces controller packets with prescribed integer row sums, and constructs and installs a reserve correcting every bounded even-total degree defect.
entries.title: Binary adjacency rank and regular induced subgraphs

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 1.4 of the paper "Structured coordinate systems in Lᵖ(ℝ)" by D. Freeman, L. Liehr and M. A. Taylor (arXiv:2610.18709v2). For every 1 ≤ p < ∞ and every ε > 0 there is a Schauder basis of Lᵖ(ℝ) that consists of non-negative functions and has basis constant less than 1 + ε, and no Schauder basis of non-negative functions has basis constant 1. For every 2 ≤ p < ∞ there are a nonzero real-valued function f ∈ Lᵖ(ℝ) and real numbers λₙ such that the translates f(· − λₙ) form a Schauder basis of Lᵖ(ℝ), over the real and over the complex scalars. For p = 2 and every ε > 0, the function f can be chosen such that it extends to an entire function and the basis constant is less than 1 + ε. For p > 2 and every unbounded set S ⊆ ℝ, the function f can be chosen non-negative and such that it extends to an entire function, with all λₙ in S.
entries.title: Structured coordinate systems in Lᵖ(ℝ)

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of Butson's theorem (1962): if a Butson-type Hadamard matrix H(p, n) exists, with p prime and n at least 2, then p divides n. A Butson-type Hadamard matrix H(k, n), for k > 0, is an n by n complex matrix whose entries are k-th roots of unity and whose rows are mutually orthogonal, M M* = n I; H(2, n) are the real Hadamard matrices. The statement and definition are those of Formal Conjectures (ButsonHadamardMatrix.lean), copied verbatim. The proof is the standard vanishing-sum argument: two orthogonal rows give a vanishing sum of n p-th roots of unity; counting how often each power of exp(2 pi i / p) occurs gives a rational polynomial of degree below p vanishing at that root, so the p-th cyclotomic polynomial 1 + X + ... + X^(p-1) divides it, every power occurs equally often, and p divides n.
entries.title: Butson's prime divisibility theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Kasteleyn's method for counting perfect matchings of plane graphs. Graphs are Mathlib simple graphs on a finite vertex type (no loops, no multiple edges); a rotation system is a permutation of the darts that cycles the darts leaving each vertex, its faces are the cycles of the face permutation, and it is plane if the graph is connected and Euler's formula |V| + |F| = |E| + 2 holds, F the set of faces. A Kasteleyn orientation with respect to a face f0 is an orientation of the edges in which every face other than f0 has an odd number of clockwise darts. Since faces are cycles of darts, a graph without edges has no faces in this representation; a connected graph without edges is a single vertex, which is not plane in this sense and is treated by a separate theorem. Five theorems are compared: (1) every rotation system of a connected graph with at least one edge has a Kasteleyn orientation with respect to any face f0; (2) for a plane rotation system, a Kasteleyn orientation and edge weights in any commutative ring, the Pfaffian of the signed weighted adjacency matrix (defined by expansion along the first row for a linear order on the vertices) equals, up to a sign +1 or -1, the sum over the perfect matchings of the products of their edge weights; (3) with unit weights the Pfaffian is plus or minus the number of perfect matchings and the determinant of the signed adjacency matrix is its square; (4) one fixed word program for an explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, natural registers and memory cells bounded by a word bound W along the run; the machine also has exact real registers, and a word program contains no instruction that uses them) computes a Kasteleyn orientation of every rotation system of a connected graph with at least one edge, with F faces and S darts, given by a standard encoding of 4 + F + 3S words, within 36F + 39S + 27 steps with every natural word at most 4F + 5S + 8; (5) a connected graph without edges has one vertex, no darts and no perfect matching, and the Pfaffian and determinant identities of (2) and (3) hold for it, both sides being 0. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Kasteleyn orientations and the Pfaffian method for plane graphs, with a linear-time orientation, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the main results of Knowles and Yin, "Anisotropic local laws for random matrices" (arXiv:1410.3516). The sample covariance matrix is Q = T X X* T* with X an M x N matrix of independent centred real entries of variance 1/N (Assumption 2.1). Proved, for real matrices and real deterministic vectors, at fixed N >= N_0 with explicit constants: the anisotropic and averaged local laws (Theorem 3.6), the law outside the spectrum (Theorem 3.7), Corollary 3.9, the rigidity of the eigenvalues (Theorem 3.12), edge universality (Theorem 3.18), the local laws for general T (Proposition 11.1), and for deformed Wigner matrices the local laws (Theorem 12.2), the rigidity of the extreme eigenvalues (Theorem 12.4) and edge universality (Theorem 12.5). No result of another work is assumed for these statements; every result that the paper uses for them is proved in the library from Mathlib.
entries.title: Anisotropic local laws for random matrices

entries.abstract: Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization resolving all four main conjectures (A, B, C, D) and the Section 6 real-positivity question from Joseph Malkoun's preprint "Finite graphs and configurations of points" (arXiv:2508.13472v3), alongside unconditional positive theorems for linear paths LG_n and small trees. Using strictly propext, Quot.sound, and Classical.choice (zero sorry, zero admit, zero native_decide), the repository formalizes: (1) a bipartite quaternionic time-reversal Gram reduction extending Malkoun's Theorem 4.1 to all finite simple bipartite graphs (MalkounBipartite); (2) formal planar homotopy disproofs of Conjectures A, B, and Section 6 on the connected K_4-barbell B_8 (MalkounCounterexample), the 7-vertex 2-vertex-connected graph H_7 = K_4 ∪_{2e} K_3 (k4e2k3Graph in MalkounN7Counterexample; smallest counterexample found in our numerical scan — absence of connected counterexamples on n <= 6 vertices is an empirical numerical-search observation, not formally proved), and the 8-vertex triangle-free 3-regular 3-vertex-connected Wagner graph M_8 (wagnerGraph in MalkounWagnerCounterexample); (3) refutations of General Conjecture D at m=6 (rank-3 matrix on C_6) and Rank-2 Spinor Conjecture D at m=12 (2x12 Gaussian-integer witness on C_{12}) alongside unconditional Conjecture C for LG_3, LG_4, K_{1,3}, and LG_5 (MalkounConjectureD); (4) an exact planar 120-degree pinwheel zero A_{T_{10}}(x) = 0 on the 10-vertex cubic cherry tree T_{10} (cherryTree10 in MalkounConjectureC) refuting Conjecture C, tree-restricted Conjecture D, and planar tree Conjectures A and B simultaneously (absence of tree violations on 4 <= n <= 9 vertices is likewise a numerical search observation, not formally proved), plus exact integer Hopf coordinates on the 15-vertex path graph pathGraphN 15 (LG_{15}) giving Re(A_{LG_{15}}) = -40605770611892600000 / 58001564658819600000 < 0; and (5) unconditional Path Conjectures B and A (|A_{LG_n}(x)| >= 1 for all n and x in C_{LG_n}(R^3)) via an exact hyperbolic SU(2) Lyapunov transfer invariant, together with unconditional Planar Path Conjecture C (Re >= 1 for all n whenever z_u = 0) (MalkounPathPositivity). Across the 12 compared declarations in Challenge.lean, six state pure existential or negative refutations whose witnesses (B_8, C_6, C_{12}, T_{10}) reside inside Solution.lean/Matematyka/, four explicitly bind the witnesses k4e2k3Graph (Fin 7), wagnerGraph (Fin 8), cherryTree10 (Fin 10), and pathGraphN 15 (Fin 15) along with coplanarity (x.1 u 2 = 0) where advertised, and two prove unconditional path positivity for all n. Topological graph planarity of H_7, vertex-transitivity of M_8, and 50-digit mpmath companion scans lie outside the formal Lean theorems.
entries.title: Counterexamples to All Four Malkoun Conjectures (A–D), Planar Tree Zeros, and Unconditional Path Positivity

entries.abstract:
We study how local changes affect waves in an infinite Ammann–Beenker network, a mathematical model with an octagonal structure.

At a particular energy, the network has two localized wave patterns, which we call A and B. An earlier theorem, registered with Palomar as PALOMAR-2026-11-06-000012, proved that these two patterns account for all independent states at that energy in the entire infinite network.

Further results proved in Lean establish that, at this special setting, no other real energy level lies within a distance of 1/128 of their common energy.

We can influence the two localized patterns in two different ways.

The first is to change a parameter that affects the first ring of the network. This raises or lowers the energy of A by exactly the parameter change, while leaving the energy of B unchanged. Both patterns remain exact eigenstates of the infinite system, without spreading outside their original localized forms. The spectral gap was proved at the original setting; for sufficiently small changes to this parameter, separation from the other energy levels also follows from the general eigenvalue-stability estimates already established in Lean.

The second is to change the strength of a single edge connecting the two rings. Here the situation is more subtle. One combination of the original patterns, called the dark state, remains protected at the original energy. The other, called the bright state, responds to the change and interacts with the rest of the infinite network.

Our main theorem proves what actually happens in this second case. For a sufficiently small, nonzero edge change, there are exactly two distinct real energy levels represented by eigenvectors in a specified narrow range. One remains fixed, while the other moves upward when the edge is strengthened and downward when it is weakened. Each level has only one independent wave pattern.

The theorem also gives two precise numerical guarantees. The moving energy differs from the original energy plus one quarter of the edge change by no more than 112 times the square of that change. For a normalized wave at the moving energy, the size of the part extending beyond the original two-state space is at most 64 times the square root of 7, multiplied by the absolute size of the edge change.

This means that we can make the external part of the moving wave as small as desired while keeping the two energy levels distinct. These are exact results for the infinite system, not predictions from a simplified two-state model.

What happens if the edge change is temporary? Separate theorems, already proved in Lean, study an edge change applied for a period of time and then switched off. They give a bound on the wave's component outside the original two-state space: no more than 512 times the absolute size of the edge change, multiplied by the initial wave's size. This bound is independent of the duration of the pulse and of the time elapsed after switching it off.

These temporal conclusions are conditional: they assume that the supplied evolution preserves norms, preserves the operator's mathematical domain, and commutes with the relevant Hamiltonian during each stage. A general physical quantum propagator has not yet been constructed in this formalization.

The results fit together in a natural way. Changing the first-ring parameter offers an exact way to adjust the relative energies of the two original patterns without changing their shapes. Changing the connecting edge produces a genuine energy separation involving a bright-derived state, while the associated spreading into the infinite network can be kept small. The temporal results complement these spectral findings by showing that, under suitable evolution assumptions, the wave remains close to the original two-state space during and after a temporary edge change.

Together, these results provide a mathematical foundation for investigating whether changes to the first-ring parameter and to the connecting edge can be combined to control localized waves. They do not yet prove that any desired mixture of the two original patterns can be prepared. The results concern the real infinite-operator model, not a separately proved classification of the complete complex spectrum.

The research direction was conceived and directed by Alessandro Odasso, who is not a mathematician. According to the maintainer, AI generated the mathematical proofs and Lean formalizations under his direction. The originality and scientific significance of these results have not yet been independently assessed.
entries.title: A One-Edge Change Splits Two Energy Levels in an Infinite Ammann–Beenker Graph

entries.abstract: A binary 192-state machine with a contextual scanner that, under consistency of first-order ZF, runs forever and has no ZF proof of its nonhalting. Arithmetic Sigma-1 soundness implies unprovability in both directions. The halting sentence expresses the literal machine's behavior in every ZF model.
entries.title: Conditional ZF-independence of the exact 192-state machine

entries.abstract: We formally verify in Lean 4 the following statement: if g : ℝ → ℝ is a continuous, integrable and totally positive function and if α, β > 0 satisfy αβ < 1, then the Gabor system {e^{2πiβnx} g(x − αm) : m, n ∈ ℤ} is a frame for L²(ℝ). This is the new implication in the solution of the frame set problem for totally positive functions, which is Theorem 1.1 of the paper "Gabor Frames of Totally Positive Functions: A Complete Characterization" by de Dios Pont, Gröchenig, Liehr, Shafkulovska and Taylor (arXiv:2608.04992).
entries.title: Gabor Frames of Totally Positive Functions

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the stretched-exponential upper bound on the probability of reducibility over the rationals for the characteristic polynomial of a symmetric matrix with independent fair upper-triangular signs.
entries.title: Irreducibility for symmetric Rademacher matrices

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the main result of the paper "Derivatives of Theta Functions and a Problem of Lyubarskii and Nes" by L. Liehr, I. Shafkulovska and M. A. Taylor (arXiv:2609.27846): if Λ = Mℤ² ⊂ ℝ² is a lattice of density D(Λ) = q/p, where p and q are coprime positive integers with q ≥ p + 2, then the Gabor system of the first Hermite function h₁(t) = t·exp(−πt²) along Λ is a frame for L²(ℝ).
entries.title: Derivatives of Theta Functions and a Problem of Lyubarskii and Nes

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization proving 29 * tau(G) <= 81 * nu(G) (tau(G) <= (81 / 29) * nu(G) ~= 2.793103 * nu(G)) for every finite simple graph G, where nu(G) is the triangle packing number and tau(G) is the triangle transversal number, strictly improving Sichen Wang's 165/59 bound (arXiv:2609.13831). Main theorem: 1 of 1 in Lean (100%); companion 32-vertex gadget checked separately in exact rational Python. Extends Wang's MIT-licensed sichen-wang/tuza-lean library with helper-arborescence coupling, unmerged colored-family covers, and opposite-edge elimination, together with non-vacuity checks nu(K_4) = 1 and tau(K_4) = 2.
entries.title: Universal 81/29 Bound for Tuza's Triangle-Cover Conjecture

entries.abstract: Yilin Liu's mathematical proof and Lean formalization establish an upper bound of n choose 2 for every n in rank three, an asymptotic forcing threshold of n choose (r - 1) at each fixed rank r at least three (Erdős #643(ii)), and the eventual exact avoiding maximum (n - 1) choose (r - 1) plus floor((n - 1)/r) at each fixed rank r at least four. This repository contains the substantive Lean development ported from Liu's September 2026 submission.
entries.title: Erdős Problem #643: Extremal Disjoint-Union Hypergraphs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of Theorem 3.1 of G. Bhowmik and L. Grimmelt, The exceptional set of the Goldbach problem, arXiv 2607.27282 v2, 2026, page 9, a result the paper attributes to Hardy and Littlewood. Let E of X be the number of even integers up to X that are not a sum of two primes. The theorem is conditional on two hypotheses, Theta < 3/4 and the zero bound at Theta: every zero of every Dirichlet L-function, for every modulus and every character, primitive or not, has real part at most Theta, stated for the zeros in the open strip 0 < Re s < 1 of Mathlib's DirichletCharacter.LFunction. Under them, for every epsilon > 0 there is a constant C with E of X at most C times X to the power 2 Theta - 1/2 + epsilon for every X >= 1. The zero bound is unproved for every Theta below 1 and false for every Theta below 1/2, since the Riemann zeta function has zeros on the critical line; the generalized Riemann hypothesis gives it at Theta = 1/2, and then the bound X to the power 1/2 + epsilon. No cited input enters: the explicit formula for psi of x and chi with a primitive character, Davenport chapter 19, the Gallagher type mean square estimates of the major and minor arcs and the zero expansion are all proved in the entry. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. Claude and Codex agents wrote the Lean code, with ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd files and two other ported files credited to their authors in PORTING.md; it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: The exceptional set of the Goldbach problem

entries.abstract:
Suzuki's screw function of the Riemann zeta function is the even function Psi defined, for t >= 0, as an archimedean profile minus the von Mangoldt weighted prime sum over n <= e^t of Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) times (t - log n); its Krein Gram kernel is G(t,u) = Psi(t) + Psi(u) - Psi(t-u). This entry uses exactly the Lean definitions of Psi and G from the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-11-14-000017 (RequestProject/V5_1.lean) and proves two results about them in Lean 4 and Mathlib.
(1) Explicit formula, unconditional. For every real t >= 0, Psi(t), viewed as a complex number, equals the unconditionally convergent sum (a tsum over the subtype of zeros) over the nontrivial zeros rho of riemannZeta, that is the zeros with 0 < Re rho < 1, of m(rho) (exp((rho - 1/2) t) - 1) / (rho - 1/2)^2, where m(rho) is the analytic order of riemannZeta at rho. This is Suzuki's zero-sum representation of the screw function (arXiv:2206.03682, Theorem 1.1(2), eq. (1.3)). In Lean: ScrewRH.Psi_eq_tsum_zeros (t : R) (ht : 0 <= t) : ((V5_1.Psi t : R) : C) = tsum over rho in Z of zeroTerm t rho.
(2) Gram positivity, conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis. Assuming Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis (as a hypothesis), for every N and every grid t : Fin N -> R, the N by N matrix (G(t_i, t_j)) is positive semidefinite in the quadratic-form sense: x^T M x >= 0 for every real vector x. In Lean: ScrewRH.screw_gram_psd_of_RH : RiemannHypothesis -> for all (N : Nat) (t : Fin N -> R), Horizon.IsPSDq (Matrix.of fun i j => V5_1.G (t i) (t j)). This is the direction RH implies positivity of Suzuki's Theorem 1.2 (that -Psi is a screw function in Krein's sense), restricted to finite grids. Both compared results use only propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice.
Combined with a Lean proof of RiemannHypothesis, (2) becomes the unconditional statement that the Gram matrix of G is positive semidefinite on every finite grid. Such a proof was announced by Levent Alpöge in November 2026 and has been reported compiled and kernel-checked by several independent parties, on Lean v4.33.1. This entry does not import that proof and makes no claim about it; result (2) is compared and verified here only as the implication from Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis.
Significance. The registered entry certifies positivity of the genuine screw kernel on explicit grids (three Gram matrices at fixed rational nodes); this entry upgrades that, conditionally on RiemannHypothesis, to every finite grid. It is to our knowledge the first Lean formalization of Suzuki's zero-sum representation of the screw function and of the direction RH implies screw-function positivity. Scope: positive semidefinite, not strictly positive definite; real test vectors (for this real symmetric kernel equivalent to Suzuki's complex condition (1.5), but the complex form is not stated); the converse direction (positivity implies RH) is not formalized; and nothing is claimed about the Riemann Hypothesis itself.
entries.title: Certified Positivity: the explicit formula for Suzuki's zeta screw function, and positive semidefiniteness of its Gram kernel on every finite grid under the Riemann Hypothesis

entries.abstract: In every positive dimension, a crystalline measure with uniformly discrete support and uniformly discrete spectrum is a finite complex linear combination of translated, modulated combs on full-rank lattices. The support and spectrum each lie in finitely many lattice translates. The lattices can differ between terms, and the nonzero atomic weights can approach zero. This gives the physical-support covering conclusion in the question of Lev and Olevskii.
entries.title: Finite modulated lattice-comb decompositions for crystalline measures

entries.abstract: This formalization concerns a binary machine with 451 working states. Under consistency of ZF plus a Berkeley cardinal, arithmetic Σ₁-soundness of ZFC plus I₀, and a proof in ZF plus a Berkeley cardinal of consistency of the specified Craig presentation of the arithmetic consequences of ZFC plus I₀, the machine never halts on the blank tape and neither halting nor nonhalting is provable in ZFC plus I₀ or ZF plus I₀.
entries.title: Conditional independence for a literal 451-state Turing machine

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of conditional forms of Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 of H. Kadiri and A. Lumley, Short effective intervals containing primes, Integers 14, 2014, A61, arXiv 1407.7902. Theorem 1.1 says that for each row of Table 2, with threshold x0 and denominator Delta, every real x > x0 has a prime p with 1 - 1/Delta times x < p < x. The three main compared results are conditional, and every cited input is an explicit hypothesis, never an axiom. The main result, corollary57_of_inputs, says that every odd n with 5 < n < 1886389443 * 4 * 10^18 is a sum of three primes, from five inputs: 1, even Goldbach up to 4 * 10^18, the verification of Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi 2014; 2, Theorem 2 of Montgomery and Vaughan 1973, the Brun Titchmarsh inequality; 3, Dusart 2010 Theorem 5.2 at eta = 0.05, the bound |theta t - t| < 0.05 t / log^2 t for t >= 122568683, from which the Costa Pereira bound that the paper cites as Lemma 2.1 is proved; 4 and 5, the paper's own numerical display 2.64, in a slightly strengthened form, at the Table 2 rows log 4 * 10^18 and 57, taken as hypotheses. The range is the row 57 range, about 4 percent below the range 1966196911 * 4 * 10^18 printed in Corollary 1.2, which uses row 60. Ternary Goldbach itself is known unconditionally by Helfgott's work, so the interest of the corollary here is the method; binary Goldbach is open. The entry also proves kl45_of_inputs, Table 2 row 45 of Theorem 1.1 in a natural number form, from inputs 2, 3 and display 2.64 at row 45, and row_of_inputs, any row of Table 2 from the Costa Pereira bound, input 2 and display 2.64 at that row. Responding to review, the entry also proves zeroError_hasSum and row_zeroError_hasSum: the weighted series over the nontrivial zeros of zeta inside zeroError is summable, with zeroError its sum, for all positive m, delta, u and X, and so at every Table 2 row at the X where display 2.64 is asked. The zero contribution in each display 2.64 hypothesis is therefore the true sum, with no summability assumption needed. AI agents, Claude by Anthropic and Codex by OpenAI, wrote the Lean code, with ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd files credited to their authors in PORTING.md; it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Short effective intervals containing primes

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the theorem of Yu. V. Linnik, Prime numbers and powers of two, Trudy Mat. Inst. Steklov 38, 1951, pages 152 to 169, in its qualitative form: conditional on the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, there is a constant K such that every sufficiently large even integer is the sum of two primes and at most K powers of two, each power 2^v with v >= 1. The one hypothesis is GRH, taken as an explicit hypothesis and never as an axiom: for every modulus q >= 1, every Dirichlet character chi modulo q and every s in the open strip 0 < Re s < 1, if the L-function of chi vanishes at s then Re s = 1/2. The constant K is not explicit. The theorem printed on page 154 is an asymptotic formula for the number of representations of N as two primes and exactly k powers of two, for each fixed k >= 3; the entry proves the qualitative consequence that Linnik draws from it on pages 168 and 169, and not the asymptotic formula itself. Linnik 1953 and Gallagher 1975 later removed the hypothesis GRH, and the gallagher1975 entry of this repository is the unconditional result. The route uses a repaired bound for the mixed integral of page 160 with log N to the power 7 in place of the power 6 printed in display 5.5, whose power 6 form the lab could not derive; the extra logarithm does not change the conclusion. Binary Goldbach, the case K = 0, is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic and Codex by OpenAI, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Prime numbers and powers of two

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization in the Euclidean plane R^2 proving: (1) every n >= 8 admits a non-collinear n-point set with every point incident to at most floor(n/2) connecting lines (self-contained across all 12 residue classes modulo 12, adapting Felsner's family for several classes and adding an explicit 8-deletion construction for n = 12k + 11, k >= 2); (2) three infinite straight-line knight-lattice families with deficit 5/2 below n/2 (n = 60s + 53 and n = 60s + 69 for all s >= 0, and n = 60s + 61 for all s >= 1); and (3) a refutation of Grunbaum's 2010 conjecture G(n) = 2 * floor(n/4) by at least 2 across four infinite congruence classes modulo 60. Companion write-ups and logged prior-work searches (arXiv, CORE, Google Scholar as of 2026-11-22, and surveys through 2025) are published at mathdiscoveries.org/results/few-lines-through-every-point and mathdiscoveries.org/results/few-lines-five-halves-short; neither the n = 12k + 11 construction nor infinite straight-line families with deficit > 3/2 were found in those logged searches, though paywalled pages 323-326 of Akiyama et al. (2011) and print monographs remain unread/unsearched.
entries.title: Strong Dirac Counterexamples for All n >= 8 and Infinite Refutation of Grunbaum's 2010 Conjecture

entries.abstract: Concrete weighted 3-CNF queries with exact model-count preservation, explicit formula/query/randomness bounds and a finite fair-bit one-sided exact-count-oracle guarantee for simple rooted Hamiltonian graphs. No machine-runtime, space, recovery or ETH conclusion.
entries.title: A verified finite oracle reduction for Hamiltonicity

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1 of Yanbo Song, The ternary Goldbach-Vinogradov theorem with almost equal Piatetski-Shapiro primes, arXiv 2012.06322 v1, 2020, with any positive margin in the window, by the deduction of Section 4 on page 9. Theorem 1 says that for 44/45 < gamma < 1 every large enough odd n is p1 + p2 + p3 with each pi a prime of the form floor of m to the power 1/gamma and |pi - n/3| <= y, for every y > n to the power 52 - 45 gamma over 8. The margin results rest on one cited input, the paper's Lemma 3, which is Theorem 3 of C. D. Pan and C. B. Pan, Goldbach Conjecture, Science Press, Beijing, 1988, taken at the exponent 7/8 as the explicit hypothesis Lemma3 7/8 and never as an axiom. From it the entry proves Theorem 1 for every window y > n to the power 52 - 45 gamma over 8 plus delta with delta > 0, and the page 9 asymptotic formula for R of n on the same windows; the paper's Lemmas 4 and 5 are proved. The exact window result also takes the transfer step of page 9 at the exact threshold, LogTransferDQ, as a second hypothesis. An independent check of the lab could not prove that transfer step at the exact threshold, since Lemma 4 holds with a loss of n to the epsilon only, so Theorem 1 at the exact window remains open here and the headline result is the margin version. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; ternary Goldbach is a theorem of Helfgott 2013. AI agents wrote the Lean code, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: The ternary Goldbach-Vinogradov theorem with almost equal Piatetski-Shapiro primes

entries.abstract: A finite randomised floating-point program computes an approximate complex Schur decomposition for every input of spectral norm at most one. For tolerance delta and requested failure probability p in (0,1/2), the joint residual and orthogonality errors are at most delta with probability at least 1-p. The program uses logarithmically many significand and natural control-word bits, and cubic work times a squared logarithm. Exact triangular storage and the work bound hold on every execution.
entries.title: Schur decomposition with logarithmic precision in cubic time up to squared logarithmic factors

entries.abstract:
This is a Lean 4 formalization of the two papers 
"Sharp isoperimetric inequalities on the Hamming cube II: The
critical exponent" by P. Durcik, P. Ivanisvili, J. Roos and X. Xie,
and "Sharp isoperimetric inequalities on the Hamming cube near the
critical exponent" by P. Durcik, P. Ivanisvili and J. Roos.
The central result of this sequence of two papers is a sharp isoperimetric
inequality on the Hamming cube at the critical exponent.
Additional results include the resolution of a conjecture of Kahn and Park on
cube partitions, a sharp L^1 Poincare inequality for Boolean-valued functions
and some improved isoperimetric inequalities for large subsets of the Hamming cube.
The structure of the formalization closely follows the structure of the paper and most
mathematical claims of the two papers are represented by Lean statements within the repository.
The Lean code was generated by coding agents.
entries.title: Formalization of sharp isoperimetric inequalities on the Hamming cube

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the main results of Yin, "The Localization Scale of the Block Anderson Model in One Dimension at Arbitrary Coupling and Volume" (arXiv:2611.09776). The model is H = (g (S + S^{-1}) tensor I_W + diag(V_1, ..., V_L)) / max{1, g} on C^L tensor C^W, with independent GUE blocks V_a of size W and the cyclic shift S of Z_L. Theorem 1.4: for 0 < kappa < 1/2 and all D, tau > 0, for all large W, every L >= 3 and every coupling g >= 0, the expected fraction of the eigenvalues in the bulk energy set J_{g,kappa,L} that are simple and whose eigenvector has localization length between W^{-tau} l and W^{tau} l, where l = min{WL, max{W, W^2 g^2}}, is at least 1 - W^{-D}. Corollary 1.5: if also L <= W^{B_L}, then with probability at least 1 - W^{-D} this holds for every eigenvalue in J_{g,kappa,L}. No result of another work is assumed; every result that the paper uses is proved in the library from Mathlib.
entries.title: The localization scale of the block Anderson model in one dimension at arbitrary coupling and volume

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization over R of the exact maximum number m(n) of open unit cubes of the n x n x n cube [0, n]^3 met by a single plane, proving m(n) = floor((9n^2 + 4n - 17)/4) for all 3 <= n <= 32 (in particular m(10) = 230, settling the open case stated by Barany and Frankl, 2021) and for all n >= 700, refuting Barany and Frankl's Section 5 "+2" remark for all n >= 700, and proving the universal upper bound m(n) <= floor((9n^2 + 6n - 20)/4) for every n >= 2. The finite intermediate window 33 <= n <= 699 is not discharged inside Lean and is certified separately by exact-integer programs documented in the accompanying paper.
entries.title: Maximum Unit Cubes Cut by a Plane in [0, n]^3 (Cheese-Cutting Theorem M)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the following theorem: a strongly continuous one-parameter group of unitary operators on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space has simple continuous spectrum if and only if one of its orbits contains a Schauder basis, that is, there are a vector g and pairwise distinct real numbers t_n such that (U_{t_n} g) is a Schauder basis.
entries.title: Schauder bases in unitary orbits

entries.abstract: Seven Lean results on robust expansion. Fixed-cardinality sampling preserves robust out-expansion with an explicit expansion parameter and failure bound. Sufficiently large robust outexpanders of linear minimum semidegree have a Hamilton cycle. Robust graphs of linear minimum degree admit spanning vertex-disjoint paths between prescribed pairs. Almost regular robust graphs admit edge-disjoint realizations of small layouts with a robust remainder. The final three results prove approximate and exact Hamilton decompositions for regular digraphs and exact Hamilton decompositions for even-regular graphs.
entries.title: Robust expanders: spanning structures and Hamilton decompositions

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization refuting McNamara and Steingrimsson's Question 9.5 (2015) via an explicit 19-element closed interval [213, 2574613] of largest rank size 7 and width 8, and proving that for every k >= 1 there exists a principal downset [empty, tau_k] whose width exceeds its largest rank size by exactly k. Companion write-up and dated prior-work searches (arXiv, CORE 2026-11-20, Google Scholar 2026-11-22, Zenodo, DataCite, HAL, OSF, and Elizalde-McNamara 2015 / Vatter 2026) are published at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/pattern-poset-not-sperner; no prior non-Sperner interval of the classical pattern poset was found in those logged searches, while Pouzet-Rosenberg (1986), Burosch et al. (1990, 1996), and print monographs remain unread/unsearched.
entries.title: Non-Sperner Intervals and Exact Deficiency Family in the Permutation Pattern Poset

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization for Graham and Harary's hypercube diameter-preserving spanning subgraph problem: proves the universal lower bound 2^n + ceil((2^n - 2n)/(n - 1)) <= f(n) for all n >= 2, raises the asymptotic second-term coefficient to 3/2 on the scale 2^n/(n - 1), and certifies 39 <= f(5) <= 40, f(6) >= 76, f(7) >= 150, f(8) >= 294, and improved lower bounds through dimension n = 32. Companion write-up and prior-work search log (including Google Scholar sweep on 2026-11-22) are published at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/hypercube-edge-bounds; no priority is claimed over unread sources (the full body of Bouabdallah-Delorme-Djelloul 1995 and Djelloul's 1993 thesis could not be accessed).
entries.title: Lower Bounds on Diameter-Preserving Spanning Subgraphs of the Hypercube

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization proving that there exists a unique permutation p of {1, ..., k} with every i + p(i) a Fibonacci number if and only if k belongs to Layman's sequence w(n) = floor(F_{n+3} / sqrt(5)) (equivalently Hajnal's M4 sequence). Formalizes Hajnal's (2022) "only if" direction and Reshetnikov's (2015, OEIS A097083) floor formula alongside a step-lemma proof of the "if" direction (Hajnal Conjecture 1). Companion write-up and dated prior-work searches (arXiv, OEIS, zbMATH, CORE 2026-11-20, Google Scholar 2026-11-22) are published at https://mathdiscoveries.org/results/fibonacci-sum-permutations; the "if" direction was not found in those logged searches (MathSciNet and print problem sections remain unsearched).
entries.title: Uniqueness Characterization of Fibonacci-Sum Permutations (Layman's Conjecture / Hajnal Conjecture 1)

entries.abstract: Unconditional Lean 4 formalization of two explicit, strictly increasing, pairwise disjoint infinite families x(m) and y(m) (m >= 0) of base-6 Lychrel numbers under repeated base-6 reverse-and-add T(n) = n + rev_6(n). Family 1 has 110 + 2m base-6 digits (smallest seed x(0) with 86 decimal digits) and Family 2 has 108 + 2m base-6 digits (smallest seed y(0) with 84 decimal digits), with middle blocks linked by base-6 digit complement d |-> 5 - d. Both satisfy the exact period-12 self-similar recurrence T^[12](x(m)) = x(m + 3) and T^[12](y(m)) = y(m + 3) while avoiding all base-6 palindromes, proving unconditionally that infinitely many base-6 Lychrel numbers exist.
entries.title: Two infinite families of base-6 Lychrel numbers

entries.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of parts of F. Najman, A. Trbović, "Splitting of primes in number fields generated by points on some modular curves" (Res. Number Theory 8 (2022)). For the 18 hyperelliptic models y² = f_N(x) of the paper (its explicit equations; their identification with the modular curves X₀(N) is not formalized), and quadratic fields ℚ(√D) generated by points with x ∈ ℚ and y ∉ ℚ: Theorem 2.2 (Table 2: primes that split, are unramified or not inert, and conditions on D), the square-residue conclusion of Theorem 2.8 (Table 3), Theorem 2.12 (infinitely many such fields in which a given prime ramifies, Table 4), and Theorem 2.13 with Table 7 in the corrected form of the authors' erratum (non-exceptional points), with the ring of integers, discriminant and residue rings of ℚ(√D). For Proposition 3.1 (complete splitting, in cubic fields K with E(K)_tors ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ/14, of primes of multiplicative reduction): the local and algebraic steps, the passage from the torsion hypothesis to a point on the model of X₁(2,14), and the splitting conclusion under an explicit hypothesis replacing the step of the paper's proof that is not formalized. Also numerical checks against an exceptional point at level 26 and the printed Lemmas 2.6(b) and 2.9. 51 theorems and 1 definition, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Splitting of primes in number fields generated by points on some modular curves (partial)

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the paper "The Double Midset Conjecture for Metric Continua" (Lucas Alves de Almeida, 22 November 2026), which proves the Loveland-Wayment conjecture: a nondegenerate compact connected metric space in which every pair of distinct points has exactly two equidistant points is homeomorphic to the circle (Theorem A). Formalized: every definition, lemma, fact (in the form used), proposition, corollary and theorem of Sections 2-12, including Theorems A, B and C, the converse (the Euclidean circle has the DMP), the characterization of the metrizable continua admitting a DMP metric, and the facts that arcs and simple triods are finite trees. Not formalized: figures, remarks and the open questions of Section 13, and R. L. Moore's general theorem behind Fact 2.5 (only its consequence "a dendrite without branch points is an arc" is proved, which is all the paper uses).
entries.title: The Double Midset Conjecture for Metric Continua

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of randomized perfect-matching and maximum-matching algorithms through the Tutte matrix, on an explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, including natural division and remainder; natural registers and memory cells bounded by a word bound W along the run). The machine also has exact real registers; both statements require the program to be a word program, containing no real instruction, so that every run uses only the bounded natural words. Two theorems are compared. (1) There is one fixed word program such that, for every simple graph G on the vertices 0, ..., n - 1 whose m edges (u, v), u < v, are listed once, every prime p and every W with W >= p^2 + p and W >= 3 n^2 + n + 3 m + 6, the program run on the input words (n, p, m, then u, v and the value x{u, v} in 0, ..., p - 1 for each listed edge) halts, for every substitution x of the indeterminates of the Tutte matrix by elements of ZMod p (a function on the unordered pairs of vertices), within 62 n^3 + 116 n^2 + 91 n + 24 n (floor(log2 p) + 1) + 27 m + 31 steps; and if G has a perfect matching, the fraction of the substitutions x for which the printed words are not the pairs of a perfect matching of G (every pair an edge, every vertex exactly once) is at most n / p. The program builds the substituted Tutte matrix, inverts it by Gauss-Jordan elimination modulo p and runs the elimination of Mucha and Sankowski with rank-two updates of the inverse. (2) There is one fixed word program such that, for every such G, p and W with W >= p^2 + p and W >= 15 n^2 + 2 n + 3 m + 6, the program run on the input words (n, p, m; for each listed edge u, v and the value z{u, v} in 0, ..., p - 1; then for all i, j < n the words i, n + j and the value z{i, n + j}) halts, for every assignment z in ZMod p to the unordered pairs of the 2n vertices of G padded with n vertices adjacent to every vertex of G, within 522 n^3 + 579 n^2 + 248 n + 60 n (floor(log2 p) + 1) + 54 m + 58 steps; and the fraction of the assignments z for which the printed words are not the pairs of a maximum matching of G (a matching with at least as many pairs as any matching of G) is at most 2n / p. This program computes the rank r of the substituted Tutte matrix of G modulo p (twice the matching number with high probability, by Lovasz's theorem), pads G with n - r vertices adjacent to every vertex, runs the elimination algorithm on the padded graph and prints the matched pairs of original vertices. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Perfect and maximum matchings by Mucha-Sankowski elimination on a word RAM, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: For exceptional three-increment directed Cayley graphs in an abelian group, under the displayed torsion, nondegeneracy and generation assumptions, the reflected pair is isomorphic exactly when the singleton and half-turn increments do not generate the ambient group. A separate theorem proves non-isomorphism for two explicit three-increment digraphs on Z/(12r)Z for every positive natural r, with no affine restriction on vertex equivalences. These are adaptations of prior public Couret formalizations; mathematical novelty and independent human review are not established.
entries.title: Directed Cayley non-isomorphism and abelian generation dichotomy

entries.abstract: Every sufficiently large N-vertex graph contains an induced subgraph of order between r and 2r−1 with a degree class of proportion at least 1−η, where r is the ceiling of K log N, for every K>0 and 0<η<1. Consequently log g(k)=o(k) for the least Caro–Yuster repetition threshold.
